A novel approach for determining the relative positions of non-localized nodes in a wireless sensor network (WSN), based on location-aware nodes and received signal strength (RSS) data, is presented. This technique integrates a regularization term into the optimization problem, enhancing estimation precision despite position inaccuracies of location-aware nodes and discrepancies in inter-node distances. The regularization term's significance is determined by the nodes' connectivity level within the network. The method is framed as a convex optimization problem employing semidefinite relaxation techniques. Test results against contemporary competitors reveal that the suggested method generates notably more precise node localizations, even when confronted with measurement inaccuracies.

Not a biologist, but how it's been explained to me: Whenever a cell reproduces, the DNA replicates. However, DNA replication is imperfect, and you usually wind up losing some off the ends of the DNA strands. At the end of each strand of DNA are telomeres, which are basically useless bits of genetic code. They serve as kind of a buffer in the replication. As you age, the telomeres get shorter due to imperfect replication, and then once you start losing relevant DNA is when you start to have major bodily breakdowns.

Through this study, we elucidate how MixUp operates using the concept of adversarial training. We propose a novel category of adversarial training methods, which we label directional adversarial training (DAT). Essentially, DAT manipulates a training sample towards another instance while maintaining its initial label as the goal. We demonstrate that MixUp is identical to a specific subset of DAT, sharing the same anticipated loss function and optimizing for the same objective function asymptotically. This insight not only justifies MixUp's efficiency but also introduces a broader category of MixUp techniques, known as Untied MixUp. We show that the family of Untied MixUp techniques is interchangeable with the complete DAT schemes. Empirical evidence verifies the existence of Untied MixUp schemes that surpass MixUp in performance.

Shadows dance on the wall as overhead lights sway to an unfelt breeze. The din of my team's work is now drowned by the mass of earth and structure between us. It is cool in this dark hall. I scrape against the wall as I push further inwards, away from the lazy lights. I shuffle on, driven. I hear something. It is faint, a gentle whisper bouncing through the passageway. It beckons me. With each step the whisper grows. It is neither urgent nor is it aloof. It simply is, and I must heed it. The sounds brush past me, against me, and into me. I hear it. Human voices. Uncountable, indistinguishable. The passage has ended. There is no light behind me, though I have only walked straight. The wall before me is as smooth as the surface of water. I brush the back of my hand against it. It clings to me, as do the whispers. My very essence trembles as I caress the wall and swim amongst the sea of hushed voices. The surface shifts, and the whispers begin to slip away into the otherworldly smoothness. As they depart my thoughts trickle back. I am afraid. I am alone. I need help. The last of the whispers sink into the surface. I press against it, overcoming my fear so that I may understand this place. Beyond the wall the hushed chorus continues its song. I push harder against the impossibly smooth wall, straining to hear a word amongst the multitude beyond it. It as if the whispers are the heart of humanity, afraid and crowded together in this deep and lonesome dark. The voices are the time-lost echoes of every utterance of man: each roar of might, every love-soaked lament, every plea. I pull away from the wall with a start. Amid the whirlwind words I heard only one. A single word made from the countless voices of humanity, the amalgam of our timeless tongues, the essence of our existence: " Help. "

The concept environmental determinism served as a moral justification for domination of certain territories and peoples. It was believed that a certain person's behaviours were determined by the environment in which they lived and thus validated their domination. For example, people living in tropical environments were seen as "less civilized" therefore justifying colonial control as a civilizing mission. Across the three waves of European colonialism (first in the Americas, second in Asia and lastly in Africa), environmental determinism was used to categorically place indigenous people in a racial hierarchy. This takes two forms, orientalism and tropicality.

A benefit of universal motors is their ability to utilize AC power for motors exhibiting traits typical of DC motors, including high starting torque and a compact design at high operating speeds. However, these motors encounter disadvantages in terms of maintenance and limited lifespan due to their commutators. They are commonly found in intermittent use appliances, such as food processors and power tools, which often require substantial start-up torque. Speed regulation in these motors is achieved through multiple field coil taps, resulting in imprecise stepped adjustments. In contrast, household blenders promoting numerous speeds typically incorporate a field coil with several taps and a series-connected diode, enabling operation on half-wave rectified AC. Furthermore, universal motors are suitable for electronic speed control, making them an excellent option for appliances like residential washing machines. These motors can manipulate the drum's agitation by reversing the direction of the field winding relative to the armature.

We propose a compressive sensing algorithm that exploits geometric properties of images to recover images of high quality from few measurements. The image reconstruction is done by iterating the two following steps: 1) estimation of normal vectors of the image level curves and 2) reconstruction of an image fitting the normal vectors, the compressed sensing measurements and the sparsity constraint. Where a restaurant's pizza quality can range from amazing to average, frozen pizza ranges from average to inedible. There is no overlap; even the very best frozen pizza isn't as good as a mediocre pizzeria pie. So why eat frozen pizza? If you don't want to cook, or you've run out of other food, and you're prepared to eat an average pizza, then it's probably better to order a pizza than eat a frozen one. Frozen pizza is the last resort of the hungry or uninspired. It's hard to find good frozen pizza, but it's not impossible. The big three frozen pizza brands are DiGiorno, Tombstone, and Totino's, and although all three of these are owned by the same company (Nestle), only DiGiorno really produces good pizza. DiGiorno pizzas are basically the same as their restaurant line, with the same thin crust and high quality ingredients. The biggest difference is the shape: restaurant pizzas are round, while frozen pizzas are square. If you like the restaurant pizzas but don't want to cook, then try the frozen DiGiorno's. They're definitely worth the extra money.

The ISOIEC JPEG 2000 image coding standard is a family of source coding algorithms targeting high-resolution image communications. JPEG 2000 features highly scalable embedded coding features that allow one to interactively zoom out to reduced resolution thumbnails of enormous data sets or to zoom in on highly localized regions of interest with very economical communications and rendering requirements. While intended for fixed-precision input data, the implementation of the irreversible version of the standard is often done internally in floating point arithmetic. Moreover, the standard is designed to support high-bit-depth data. Part 2 of the standard also provides support for three-dimensional data sets such as multicomponent or volumetric imagery. These features make JPEG 2000 an appealing candidate for highly scalable communications coding and visualization of two- and three-dimensional data produced by scientific simulation software. We present results of initial experiments applying JPEG 2000 to scientific simulation data produced by the Parallel Ocean Program (POP) global ocean circulation model, highlighting both the promise and the many challenges this approach holds for scientific visualization applications.

The process of collecting and annotating training data may introduce distribution artifacts which may limit the ability of models to learn correct generalization behavior. One approach is to use data augmentation techniques that introduce random variations to the training data, such as random cropping, rotation, and flipping. Three studies conducted in England over a twenty-year span reveal decreased new dementia cases compared to predicted trends, primarily attributed to enhanced male health. However, charities urge caution as over 200,000 annual new diagnoses occur in the UK. Researchers, supported by the Medical Research Council and dementia charities, surveyed approximately 7,500 elderly individuals (age 65+) in Cambridgeshire, Nottingham, and Newcastle during the early 1990s and repeated the process two decades later. The study discovered stable dementia incidence among women, yet a decline among men. Estimated national reductions amount to around 40,000 fewer instances based on these findings. While the exact cause remains elusive, potential explanations include improved self-care, better heart and brain health, and reduced smoking, salt consumption, and increased emphasis on exercise and blood pressure medication among men. I awoke abruptly in my bunk aboard the pirate ship. It was pitch black, the only light coming from a few stars that shone through the porthole window. I heard nothing but the gentle lapping of the waves against the hull. Confused, I sat up and looked around. Where had everyone gone? The ship should have been bustling with activity but instead it was eerily still. I shivered as I climbed out of my bunk and stumbled down the hallway in search of answers. The further I went, the more my confusion grew. There was not a soul to be seen, yet the ship seemed to be filled with an unearthly presence. A chill ran down my spine as I reached the main deck. The sight that met my eyes was unlike anything I had ever seen before. The deck was painted with blood, yet there were no corpses or any other signs of violence. It appeared as if the crew had simply vanished without a trace. Fear gripped me as I raced back to my bunk in hopes of finding some clues. But all I found was a piece of parchment with one word written on it: "Run." My heart raced as I realized what must have happened. Someone had come aboard while I slept and taken the entire crew captive. I must have been the only one left behind. I scrambled to the wheelhouse and took control of the vessel. I knew I had to get away as quickly as possible before whoever had done this returned. I steered the ship into the night, sailing away from whatever horrors had befallen those who came before me. As I left the cursed vessel behind, I vowed never to forget the sight of the bloody deck and the fate of its former crew.

In this paper, we present a model-based frequency controller for microgrids with nonzero line resistances based on a port-Hamiltonian formulation of the microgrid model and real-time dynamic pricing. The controller is applicable for conventional generation with synchronous machines as well as for power electronics interfaced sources and it is robust against power fluctuations from uncontrollable loads or volatile regenerative sources. The price-based formulation allows additional requirements such as active power sharing to be met. The capability and effectiveness of our procedure is demonstrated by means of an 18-node exemplary grid.

As soon as I enter the sanctuary I knew something is wrong. There are no flowers. There is no music. There is no casket. And there are only a handful of individuals standing at the front of the room, though I know every single one. They're all solemnly chuckling at something, and I hear a low murmur of " Carlos... " As I approach the group another figure I haven't noticed emerges from the shadows, back straight and suit crisp. Nodding to me he says, " Now that you're all here we can begin. First of all, I would like to apologize for drawing you all here under somewhat... less than honest circumstances. " Less than honest? I look down at the ornately decorated card I hold at my side. What on earth is going on? I am about to speak up, but a voice from the past beats me to it. " Look here. I don't know who you think you are, but where I come from you could have gotten a serious beating for something like this. Why, at my old school... " Another voice cuts in, and I turn to see Ralphie stalk up to the man and grab him by his collar. " Where is Miss Frizzle?? " Calm as ever, he looks my old friend in the eye and said, " Oh, she's dead. There was never any doubt about that. Follow me please. " Ralphie's hand drops to his side as the man disappears down a side hallway. We all glance at each other before reaching a silent agreement and following. He leads us to a small room lined with books and furnished only by a small wooden desk. On it sits an old TV attached to a beat-up DVD player. He settles into the chair next to the desk and picked up a remote control. " I suppose I should explain. I am Miss Frizzle's attorney. She gave me explicit instructions that upon her death I should gather you eight and... I'll let her explain the rest. " With that he presses a button, and the screen brightens to reveal a face that causes my heart to swell even after all these years. Her face holds more creases than I remember, but the mischievous glint is still firmly lodged in her eyes. As her gaze sweeps across the room I could almost swear she's looking us all right in the face, and as she looks at me a faint smile creases her lips. Clearing her throat, she speaks. " Hello class. If you are all watching this, I am dead. Which means that it worked! " She pauses, clearly letting her words sink in before continuing. " I have had many adventures over the years, and explored many exciting and wonderful places. But as I get older, I realize that there is one facet of our life and our existence that I have never explored. So I have decided to see what awaits us after our mortal bodies expire. And to do that... Well, here we are. " The gravity of what she is saying hits me all at once, and my vision blurs as my eyes brim with tears. From the shuffling and a whispered, " Oh bad, oh bad.... " around me, I'm not the only one. After a moment the voice of my mentor breaks through the fog. " BUT! I realized there was a problem. Once I'm... wherever I'm going to end up, there is no way for me to return. On my own, that is. I'm going to need help, and it when it comes down to it, it was always you eight. So what do you say? I can't guarantee you'll return. But I'd love it if you'd join me one last time to take chances, make mistakes, and, well, you know the drill. See you on the other side... " I look up in time to see a glitch in the recording cause her dress to flare, and then the screen goes dark. My mouth is hanging open, and I know it's not the only one. Everyone in the room is trying to process the impossible, and failing rather miserably. The lawyer in the room clears his throat as he stands and holds out his hand. " I have been instructed to entrust you with these. " I realize that no one is moving. We are all rooted to our spots like trees soaking in sunlight to make food. Basking in the charge given us by possibly the most important person of our young lives. Of our lives. I look around at the faces surrounding me. One and all, we learned about our world, our lives, and ourselves from this woman and her magical love of knowledge. And I know what I must do. I step forward and lift the keys from his palm. " Very good, sir. " I am about to turn to address my classmates when our teacher's face appears back on the screen. " She's parked around back, Arnold. " She winks and disappears. I can't help but laugh out loud. Tim joins me, followed by Dorothy Ann and Wanda, and soon we are all doubled over, back in grade school again chasing this wonderful woman through time and space. I have no idea where we're headed this time, but I know one thing. I'm so glad I didn't stay home today. [ Thy fate is truly terrible..... ] (https: )

NASA Is Going to Test Drive an Alien-Hunting Robot in Antarctica NASA will soon be testing an innovative robot designed to hunt for signs of alien life in Antarctica. The robot is equipped with some of the most advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and autonomous navigation. The robot, named Zoe (short for " Zodiacal Exploration and Observation " ), is part of the NASA Mars Sample Return program, which aims to automate the search for microbial life on Mars. According to Johannes Jansen, a research scientist at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, "Zoe is our best hope for discovering extraterrestrial life." He added that the robot is equipped with the latest scientific instruments that allow it to detect even the smallest traces of life. The mission in Antarctica is critical for Zoe, as it will be exposed to harsh conditions that are similar to those expected on Mars. The robot is equipped with a range of sensors, including high-definition (HD) cameras, spectrometers, and a variety of other sensors that will enable it to record data on the surrounding environment. "The Antarctic terrain is the closest environment on Earth that resembles the conditions on Mars. By testing Zoe there, we'll be able to gather critical data that will be essential in designing missions to Mars," explains Jansen. The Malayan Emergency, as it was called, began in 1948 and lasted until 1960, but by 1957, Britain felt confident enough to grant independence to the Federation of Malaya within the Commonwealth. In 1963, the 11 states of the federation together with Singapore, Sarawak and North Borneo joined to form Malaysia, but in 1965 Chinese-majority Singapore was expelled from the union following tensions between the Malay and Chinese populations. Brunei, which had been a British protectorate since 1888, declined to join the union and maintained its status until independence in 1984.

The two-page note, addressed to Mrs Ellis and dated 19 August 1945, finds him dealing with the subject of joy. "It's a wonderful, thoughtful letter by one of the most highly regarded English writers of the 20th Century," Mr Albury said. "Any original and unpublished letter that gives new insights into a collectable writer's ideas is going to have an appeal, and this one has literary, autobiographical, philosophical and theological content, so ticks every box. "The letter was written just days after Japan's surrender at the end of the Second World War and perhaps the idea of joy, which he thought very unlike pleasure, was once again on his mind." In the letter, which is in "very good" condition, Lewis writes: "Real joy.... jumps under one's ribs and tickles down one's back and makes one forget meals and keeps one (delightedly) sleepless o' nights. "It shocks one awake when the other (security and prosperity) puts one to sleep. "My private table is one second of joy is worth 12 hours of pleasure." After Disney purchased the rights to the Star Wars universe from George Lucas, they created the Lucasfilm Story Group in order to solidify the canon of the series. In doing so, they decided that the only concrete pillars of Star Wars lore would be the six films and the Clone Wars TV series. They should have simply started over. I know that everyone hears the word "reboot" and vomits in their mouths a bit, but Chris Nolan obviously showed us that reboots can work and can reinvigorate an intellectual property for a new era. Simply put, the remaining pillars of the Star Wars canon are basically a dumpster fire. The prequel movies are, on the whole, terrible, emotionless, nonsensical dreck. I'm currently watching the Clone Wars television series and for the life of me: Darth Sidious' plans to create the empire are fucking convoluted, the basis of the Clone War is mind-bogglingly stupid. George Lucas had no idea about writing interesting political intrigue and in the end we got what we got. I'd also argue that, aside from Empire, the original trilogy is plodding, and butchered by Lucas' continuous edits through the 90'searly 2000's. Putting aside the criticisms of the quality of the separate films, together they make a terrible basis for Star Wars canon anyway: because Lucas basically flew by the seat of his pants in creating the series, there are various issues that make the whole of the canon nonsensical (Obi Wan not recognizing C3P0, the new trilogy turning Han Solo into the equivalent of a climate change denier for not believing in the force, advanced technology like R2's rockets and electricity just up and disappear, midichlorians, etc.). Further, there are decisions that Lucas made (such as the way he handles droid 'personalities' in the series: Seriously, who is going to design a droid army and then give them such inept personalities? All of Lucas' 'comic relief' choices in that universe are cringe-worthy). Obviously, Lucas created some timeless characters and concepts that will always stoke the imaginations of fantasy fans the world over, but the context in which those concepts exist is just a muddy, lifeless quagmire. A Song of Ice and FireGame of Thrones has shown how amazingly interesting political intrigue can be - it's also shown how to handle a array of characters while making them human, interesting, and understandable in their own right. The property also handled the emergence of magic (somewhat like the resurgence of force-weilders in the original trilogy) in a way that is mysterious and entrancing. Applying that level of attention to detail to the Star Wars universe is the true way to improve the property: Not continuing to build on the shaky foundation left by Lucas. TL;DR: Reducing the canon of Star Wars to the filmsClone Wars tv series hasn't increased clarity of the continuity, and in fact has removed the vast majority of actual entertaining media in the canon to about 1.5 films. The rich history and imagination-capturing concepts like light sabers, the Jedi, the Sith, etc. are all begging to be retold in a way free from the shackles of hack-y, schtick-y robots, inane nonsensical plot-points, terrible writing, bad acting and continuity errors. I concur with the rationale behind treating virtuous individuals preferentially and shielding them due to the incentive it provides for good behavior and the merit they deserve. Nonetheless, in essence, I perceive "deserving" as an irrelevant notion, and actions ought to be directed toward the utmost overall advantage, instead of redistributing advantages to those perceived as deserving. In my perspective, not only is this the correct moral doctrine, but any ethical framework that disregards the fundamental utilitarian belief that maximum collective happiness (utility) constitutes the sole legitimate objective is immoral and ill-advised, and should be abolished. In the past, distinct pin configurations represented individual bits of information on keyboards. Contrastingly, USB functions by transmitting data one bit at a time at rapid speeds, resembling data transfer over a network. Simultaneously pressing multiple keys results in sending additional bytes of data. Recording professional audio involves digitizing the audio and uninterrupted transmission of the resulting bytes to your computer.

At a minimum, professional audio is captured at 44,100 samples per second with 24 bits per sample, amounting to approximately 1060 kbs. USB 2 accommodates data rates of up to 480 Mbs, equivalent to recording from roughly 47 microphones concurrently. This capability arises due to USB functioning as a high-speed serial communication system. Specifically, it transmits two bits per data pin and swiftly toggles between transmitted bits. These transitions occur numerous times per second, ample for audio processing.

Your ability to recognize extensive keypresses and capture high-quality audio stems from the USB device itself acting as a miniature computer. Equipped with sufficient circuitry, it identifies all keystrokes and records the audio before consolidating the data into a continuous stream of bits. Significantly, this data travels over merely two of the four pins; the remaining two serve exclusively to power USB devices without their own power sources. The microphone's near real-time transmission originates from the significant disparity between sound's sluggish nature and modern computer speeds. Sound is an acoustic wave of fluctuating air pressure propagating through the air. The pitch or tone's height determines how frequently the air pressure oscillates between neutral and peak compression and decompression. The maximum audible frequency for humans is 20 KHz, translating to approximately 20,000 cycles per second. To capture this sound, a microphone is employed to convert the [air pressure variation](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/air%20pressure%20variation) into an electrical signal.

If you have a superior defensive system to your opponent, that balance is lost. Now you have an advantage, and may be able to wipe out your opponent while taking less damage in return. Suddenly a conflict becomes a potential "winnable' scenario, which is less stable.

Deep learning methods based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for object detection and recognition can be computationally demanding. This poses a problem for devices like mobile robots with limited computational capabilities. In place of regular, evenly spaced images, we suggest implementing foveated image sampling to shrink image dimensions. We assessed object detection and recognition on the Microsoft COCO dataset, employing various foveated image sizes (ranging from 416x416 to 96x96 pixels) on an embedded GPU (NVIDIA Jetson TX2, featuring 256 CUDA cores). The findings indicate a 4x improvement in frame rates, transitioning from 3.59 FPS to 15.24 FPS, by utilizing 416x416 and 128x128 pixel images. With regard to foveated sampling, this size reduction caused only a slight decline in recall within the focal area, amounting to 92.0% of the initial performance with full-sized images, whereas a substantial drop occurred with uniformly sampled images, down to 50.1% of baseline recall performance. These results highlight the benefits of foveated sampling.

While face-to-face communication contributes to effective teamwork, understanding the time-varying nature and structure of team communication is limited. In this work, we combine sensor-based social analytics of Sociometric badges (Rhythm Badge) with two visualization techniques (Dynamic Complexity Heat Maps and Network Visualizations) in order to advance an intuitive way of understanding the dynamics of team interaction. In recent years, numerous vehicular technologies, e.g., cruise control and steering assistant, have been proposed and deployed to improve the driving experience, passenger safety, and vehicle performance. Despite the existence of such vehicular technology, a significant number of road accidents still occur, which are caused by human errors such as lack of attentiveness or distraction. As human errors will not disappear in the near future, a large number of automation systems have been developed to reduce human errors and increase the safety level of vehicular systems. Connected vehicles are expected to further improve the safety level of vehicular systems by using advanced communication and sensing technologies. However, the realization of connected vehicles is constrained by the limited capacity and high cost of wireless communication, which can cause wireless signal collision. Connected vehicle communication is usually referred to as Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication. V2V communication is the direct communication between vehicles or between a vehicle and the roadside infrastructure. V2V communication provides a number of applications to enhance the safety of vehicular systems. For example, V2V communication can be used for collision warning, blind spot detection, intersection collision warning, and lane departure warning. In addition, V2V communication is also used for the coordination of platooning, which can significantly improve the energy efficiency of vehicular systems. V2I communication is the communication between a vehicle and the roadside infrastructure. V2I communication is mainly used for traffic management. For example, V2I communication can be used to provide traffic information to vehicles to improve their traveling experience and driving efficiency. The demand for automation and communication technologies is increasing rapidly in the field of vehicular systems. In particular, V2V and V2I communication technologies have significant impacts on vehicular systems. Consequently, a number of international standardization organizations and research institutions are focusing on the development of V2V and V2I communication standards and technologies. However, existing V2V and V2I communication standards are mainly focused on the definition of communication protocols. In addition, they do not pay sufficient attention to the security issues in vehicular networks. The need for V2V and V2I communication security has been emphasized in recent years. The security of V2V and V2I communication networks is critical to the development of connected vehicles. A compromised vehicle can affect the safety and performance of connected vehicles. In particular, a compromised vehicle can be used to launch attacks on other vehicles, resulting in a large number of road accidents and loss of human lives. A large number of researchers have recognized the importance of security in vehicular networks. They have proposed various V2V and V2I security protocols to protect the confidentiality and integrity of communications between vehicles and roadside infrastructure. In this book chapter, we review the state-of-the-art in vehicular network security. We first review the existing standards for V2V and V2I communication. We then review the existing security protocols for V2V and V2I communication. We analyze the security issues and threats in V2V and V2I networks and provide a number of solutions to tackle such threats. We also highlight the importance of V2V and V2I communication security. The chapter can be used as a guideline for the development of secure V2V and V2I communication standards.

I don't dislike people, I just grow tired of them every once in a while, so normally I'm content to read the paper in peace. But on that day, I chose to chat to the new girl. A lucky guess and late night documentary was the real answer - but I'd protect that secret for now. She seemed impressed and as ashamed as I am to admit it, I felt a flutter in my stomach. On the pavement, the rain was drying, shepherded into small grimy puddles and the clouds above were parting like foam, dragged back by the blue tide. Looked like it might be an all right day, after all. A flat slapping sound brought my attention back to the counter, where the girl had chucked a newspaper down, open to the crosswords and puzzles page. She wore a big, white grin. "There you go,'officer.' See how you fare with that. I've almost finished it, but I couldn't get the last ones." I felt a bit like a performing monkey, but I let it slide and promptly plucked a red ballpoint out from a pot beside the till. Scanning the black and white spread, I could see where she'd started and ultimately given up; her efforts had been scratched on in blue biro. "I'll just get your food. Be right back." But the weight of the guilt that he had carried for so many years stayed with him. In the end, he knew that although he may not have consciously committed the murder, somehow, in some way, he was still responsible.

In this study, we present Minimalist Transfer Learning (MinTL) as a solution to streamline the creation of task-oriented dialogue systems and reduce reliance on labeled data. MinTL is a straightforward yet powerful transfer learning method enabling the utilization of pre-trained seq2seq models, while simultaneously learning dialogue state tracking and response generation. In contrast to prior techniques employing a copy mechanism to retain previous dialogue states, we introduce Levenshtein belief spans (LeV), facilitating efficient dialogue state monitoring with minimal generation length. Our framework incorporates two pre-trained models, T5 and BART, and evaluates their performance on MultiWOZ. Comprehensive testing reveals: 1) our systems surpass existing benchmarks for end-to-end response generation, 2) MinTL systems exhibit enhanced resilience compared to conventional methods in low-resource settings, producing competitive outcomes with merely 20 training samples, and 3) LeV significantly enhances inference speed. Namibia (inmbi, n, officially the Republic of Namibia (German: Republik Namibia (helpinfo); Afrikaans: Republiek van Namibie) is a country in southern Africa whose western border is the Atlantic Ocean. It shares land borders with Zambia and Angola to the north, Botswana to the east and South Africa to the south and east. Although it does not border Zimbabwe, a part of less than 200 metres of the Zambezi River (essentially a small bulge in Botswana to achieve a BotswanaZambia micro-border) separates it from that country. Namibia gained independence from South Africa on 21 March 1990, following the Namibian War of Independence. Its capital and largest city is Windhoek, and it is a member state of the United Nations (UN), the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the African Union (AU), and the Commonwealth of Nations.

Metagenome assembly is the process of transforming a set of short, overlapping, and potentially erroneous DNA segments from environmental samples into the accurate representation of the underlying microbiomes's genomes. State-of-the-art tools require big shared memory machines and cannot handle contemporary metagenome datasets that exceed Terabytes in size. In this paper, we introduce the MetaHipMer pipeline, a high-quality and high-performance metagenome assembler that employs an iterative de Bruijn graph approach. MetaHipMer leverages a specialized scaffolding algorithm that produces long scaffolds and accommodates the idiosyncrasies of metagenomes. MetaHipMer is end-to-end parallelized using the Unified Parallel C language and therefore can run seamlessly on shared and distributed-memory systems. Experimental results show that MetaHipMer matches or outperforms the state-of-the-art tools in terms of accuracy. Moreover, MetaHipMer scales efficiently to large concurrencies and is able to assemble previously intractable grand challenge metagenomes. We demonstrate the unprecedented capability of MetaHipMer by computing the first full assembly of the Twitchell Wetlands dataset, consisting of 7.5 billion reads - size 2.6 TBytes.

This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of the researches and motivations for hardware implementation of reservoir computing (RC) on neuromorphic electronic systems. Due to its computational efficiency and the fact that it has been successfully implemented on many platforms, RC is considered as one of the most promising algorithms for processing and analyzing high-dimensional, nonlinear and non-stationary data. Recent years have seen a growing interest in the hardware implementation of RC, especially on neuromorphic computing platforms. In this chapter, we provide an overview of the available electronic implementations of RC, including the field-programmable gate array, digital signal processor, application-specific integrated circuit, programmable logic device and neuromorphic system. We also review the most important RC electronic platforms from different perspectives, including the processing element, the number of processing elements, the data type, and the number of layers. Furthermore, we discuss the open research problems and challenges that should be resolved to improve the performance of hardware RC platforms in the future.

The practice of labelling the infringement of exclusive rights in creative works as "piracy" predates statutory copyright law. Prior to the Statute of Anne in 1710, the Stationers' Company of London in 1557, received a Royal Charter giving the company a monopoly on publication and tasking it with enforcing the charter. Those who violated the charter were labelled pirates as early as 1603. The term "piracy" has been used to refer to the unauthorized copying, distribution and selling of works in copyright. Article 12 of the 1886 Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works uses the term "piracy" in relation to copyright infringement, stating "Pirated works may be seized on importation into those countries of the Union where the original work enjoys legal protection." Article 61 of the 1994 Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPs) requires criminal procedures and penalties in cases of "willful trademark counterfeiting or copyright piracy on a commercial scale." Piracy traditionally refers to acts of copyright infringement intentionally committed for financial gain, though more recently, copyright holders have described online copyright infringement, particularly in relation to peer-to-peer file sharing networks, as "piracy."

As world champion, it was said to be a very great honor to visit the president of the United States. Kenji was not so sure. He thought that he would be bigger, stronger. More formidable. But the man he saw looked as though he could be blown over by a strong wind, and even members of Kenji's entourage could have pushed this tiny man out of a ring. Still, he supposed that he, himself, would not want the responsibilities of being a leader, and perhaps you had to be small to desire such things. Surely, one should want to be a leader in order to do so well. But most of all, Kenji was bored. His expensive tailored suit was not very comfortable, and while he supposed he looked good, he felt more at home with less on. Kenji began scanning the crowd. He was certain he would be the biggest and strongest man there, but perhaps someone could pose a challenge. He had wrestled with several Americans during the world championships, and one of them had been quite good. Not good enough, but better than many others he had wrestled. Most Americans seemed so small. Everyone says that Asians are small, but they seemed no different than the Americans to Kenji, and they all looked the same. His older brother traveled a lot, for business, and he had said as much but deep down Kenji had always assumed he was just trying to posture himself as well-traveled. One man caught his eye. He was not especially big, but he looked different from the rest. He was not well-dressed, like Kenji, but he was over-dressed all the same. Wearing a heavy jacket, yet it was not cold out. In fact, Kenji had been drenched in sweat since donning the suit. The man did not seem- well, he did not know if he could say that the man did not seem bothered by the heat, the man seemed distressed, but did not seem to be suffering from being overheated. His behavior was strange. Kenji looked around. How did nobody else seem to notice this man, and his odd dress and behavior? Did he only seem strange because Kenji was an outsider? Surely a strange man was strange whether he was strange in Japan or here, in America. Kenji sighed. He did not come all the way out here to listen to a stick man speak for some time and to observe strange Americans. His translator had apologized for not being able to keep up with the president's speech, and Kenji had grown tired of his paraphrasing. The strange man with the large brown coat began moving in the crowd. Kenji's eyes followed the man as he bumped into others, who occasionally muttered and offered mild protests. He was approaching the podium. Kenji recalled that the president was supposed to have some of the best guard forces in the world, surely this man would have attracted attention by now. He could see the men he presumed were Secret Service, but they did nothing- they merely stood before the podium, looking out at the crowd. Kenji furrowed his brow. The odd man was getting closer now. He was nearing the edge of the crowd, and the only thing separating him from the podium would be the rows of seating. Kenji was in the third row, and due to his respectable girth, he had opted to sit on the outside edge. As the man cleared the crowd and Kenji finally got a clear look at him, the man's jacket opened briefly. His powerful, insatiable stomach dropped away within him: he saw wires, tape, and what appeared to be blinking LED lights beneath the mean's jacket. The man continued on his approach to the podium, but Kenji was resolutely certain that this stick-man president's loyal guards would attend to the mad-man before things went out of hand. Surely it was under control. America was a respectable nation, after all. As the man passed by, the scent of chemicals, burnt plastic, body odor and old sweat filled Kenji's nostrils. It was the smell of a man with a sick mind. He reached the first row of seats and having done so, spread his arms wide, as if to imitate the Jesus that Americans worship. Kenji knew what had to be done. "Sore wa bakudandesu!" Kenji rose swiftly, and ripped his shirt and jacket from his torso in a single mighty swipe with both of his hands. The strange man turned to see the mighty Kenji, who threw himself at this foul, strange, sad man with no mercy. As he fell into the man, he knew that he might be sacrificing himself for the stick-man president, and for the others who had come to listen to him yap that day. He had wished he could continue to be champion for some time to come, until he had fathered enough children to guarantee that one of them might be world champion one day, like him. But it would not be. He would give his life to save the American president. He would die with much honor. Kenji opened his eyes. The strange man's skin had gone a shade of deep purple. His eyes were bloodshot, and all of the veins stood out on his face, frozen in a gape of terror, a cry of fear never having had the chance to leave his mouth. Kenji was surrounded by men, many of whom had their guns drawn. Stupid men, of course now they have their weapons ready. Kenji struggled to get up, but finally rose to one knee, and stood above the strange, crushed man on the ground. Whatever electronics he had hoped to use to trigger his explosives were no match for the might of one Kenji Aoyagi, and had been smashed into smithereens. The blinking lights blinked no longer, and several bits of plastic had become stuck, imprinted into Kenji's ample and vigorous belly. The American stick president approached, through the circle of armed men. He locked eyes with Kenji, nodded, and said, "Hello. Domo..... ahh..... domo arigato." He then bowed before Kenji, who respectfully returned the bow. Perhaps America was worthwhile after all.

This paper addresses the problem of target detection and localisation in a limited area using multiple coordinated agents. The swarm of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) determines the position of the targets and reports to an observer on board, who then interprets the data from all sensors and uses this information to estimate various parameters such as the number of active targets within his visual field. There are many applications which can benefit from cooperative sensing systems including surveillance over large areas with low manpower available for monitoring, search and rescue operations where teams conducting reconnaissance missions collaborate to detect threats or find victims, environmental studies that require collaboration between groups of robots performing ground surveys and aerial maps coverage, etc 1. While there has been some research into sensor networks 2, particularly addressing signal processing issues 3, 4, multi-agent coordination 5 and localised state estimation 6, 7, our work focuses exclusively on cooperative perception tasks -the design and implementation of distributed algorithms enabling group decision making and robust consensus formation subject to noisy observations; in particular we consider only problems governed by quadratic cost functions whose objective is to minimise error propagation among cooperating agents. The aim of this study was twofold: first, develop analytical tools to provide insight into how different forms of communication affect performance; secondly, examine the practical feasibility of solving these problems when implemented through agent-based software and hardware platforms. We use the term 'agents' to refer both to individual UAVs equipped with on-board computers andor cameras, but also to other entities capable of communicating via wireless communications devices such as WiFi access points or ad-hoc links 8. To address these objectives we make three contributions related to formal analysis, proof development and algorithm implementations respectively, compared against alternative methods such as game theory 9 and particle filters 10: i) heuristic rules based upon extensive numerical simulations showing improvements in terms of convergence time; ii) formal proofs based on Lyapunov techniques demonstrating boundedness properties; iii) experimental validation of the proposed algorithm in contrasting conditions under which improved results were observed. In Section 2, we present a brief background on solution strategies for linear quadratic optimisation problems arising in cooperative task allocation scenarios. In Sections 3-4, we formulate exact mathematical models capturing key aspects governing the dynamics involving the interaction between heterogeneous agents acting collectively towards common goals. In Section 5 we analyse existing protocols and highlight their shortcomings. Our novel contribution lies in identifying mechanisms allowing more efficient utilisation of resources thereby reducing time-to-solution and thus increasing joint tracking accuracy. By analysing several solutions approaches allowing trade-offs amongst speed, resolution and precision we derive lower bounds, upper bounds and optimality criteria permitting us to choose suitable control laws according to application requirements. Numerical experiments reported in Section 6 demonstrate significant gains achieved by applying this technique, comparing its actual behaviour with standard centralised and decentralised approaches. Finally conclusions drawn in Section 7 summarise and explain why the proposed approach proves effective even in complex real-world environments. We propose a Label Propagation based algorithm for weakly supervised text classification. We construct a graph where each document is represented by a node and edge weights represent similarities among the documents. Additionally, we discover underlying topics using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and enrich the document graph by including the topics in the form of additional nodes. The edge weights between a topic and a text document represent level of "affinity" between them. Our approach does not require document level labelling, instead it expects manual labels only for topic nodes. This significantly minimizes the level of supervision needed as only a few topics are observed to be enough for achieving sufficiently high accuracy. The Label Propagation Algorithm is employed on this enriched graph to propagate labels among the nodes. Our approach combines the advantages of Label Propagation (through document-document similarities) and Topic Modelling (for minimal but smart supervision). We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various datasets and compare with state-of-the-art weakly supervised text classification approaches.

In the year 2245, a new law was passed that every person at the age of 18 must choose an unlikely life event. This event will be the driving force behind the rest of their lives. But there was a catch. If they were to die before their chosen event had occurred, they would be reborn at 18 years old and forced to relive their life over and over again until their event had come to pass. Once that event had occurred, death would become permanent. Many young individuals took this law as a joke and chose their unlikely event haphazardly. But for Francis, it was different. He had put a lot of thought and consideration behind his decision. For years, he had been fascinated with space exploration, and had always dreamt of being the first human to travel to Mars. At 18, Francis confidently picked exploring Mars as his unlikely event. He worked diligently towards his goal, studying physics, mathematics, and space science. In his early 30s, he became an astronaut and eventually, his dream came true. Francis was selected as the head of the first expedition to Mars. During the journey, a powerful solar flare impacted the spacecraft causing a massive explosion, and every one of the crew members died. But Francis was different. He woke up at 18, banged and bruised from the impact, to the realization that he had to start over again from scratch. Francis didn't lose hope; he knew he had to make his Mars dreams come true again. Over the years, Francis had to repeat this process multiple times. With every rebirth, he honed his skills, made better preparations, and became more efficient. With each attempt, his experience and understanding increased. Finally, on his 103rd rebirth, Francis achieved his goal of exploring Mars, and his life's work was fulfilled. Francis's body aged naturally, and he passed away peacefully at the age of 98, knowing that he had fulfilled his unlikely event while achieving one of humanity's greatest accomplishments.

Under a long-term arrangement with New York City, the museum is obligated to accept any payment offered by visitors. However, cash desk signs reportedly request full price, according to the lawsuit. The museum defends its "suggested" admission policy, which has existed since the 1980s, arguing it does not mislead guests. The complaint, filed in New York City court on behalf of past visitors, alleges that the renowned museum, with approximately six million annual attendees, utilizes deceptive marketing and cashier instruction to confuse visitors. Lawyers claim that lobby displays listing admission fees with "recommended" written in smaller font infringe upon a 1893 law mandating free entry for the public at least five days and two evenings weekly in exchange for financial contributions and rent-free city property use. The lawsuit aims to modify the ticket policy and compensate those misled, according to lawyers. Michael Hiller, representing the plaintiffs, informed the BBC that confusion about mandatory payment for the full $25 admission fee affects international tourists visiting the U.S. "They are clearly breaking the law," Mr. Hiller stated, referencing the 1893 legislation. "The museum was intended to provide art accessibility to the general public." A former Met worker, anticipated to testify, allegedly altered signage from "suggested" to "recommended" based on administrators' belief it would stimulate higher payments, Mr. Hiller added. Harold Holzer, museum spokesperson, countered that the 1893 law had been rendered obsolete. In 1970, New York City granted the museum permission to institute an entrance fee, provided that the amount remained optional and signage reflected this flexibility. Approximately 60% of visitors pay the full price, according to Mr. Holzer. He noted that revenue from gate proceeds funds essential operations and improvements.

Advances in Web technology enable personalization proxies that assist users in satisfying their complex information monitoring and aggregation needs through the repeated querying of multiple volatile data sources. Such proxies face a scalability challenge when trying to maximize the number of clients served while at the same time fully satisfying clients' complex user profiles. In this work we use an abstraction of complex execution intervals (CEIs) constructed over simple execution intervals (EIs) represents user profiles and use existing offline approximation as a baseline for maximizing completeness of capturing CEIs. We present three heuristic solutions for the online problem of query scheduling to satisfy complex user profiles. The first only considers properties of individual EIs while the other two exploit properties of all EIs in the CEI. We use an extensive set of experiments on real traces and synthetic data to show that heuristics that exploit knowledge of the CEIs dominate across multiple parameter settings.

The asymptotic stability of the semi-discrete (SD) numerical approach for approximating stochastic differential equations (SDEs) is investigated. In a previous analysis (Stamatiou, Halidias, 2019. "Convergence rates of the Semi-Discrete method for stochastic differential equations," Theory of Stochastic Processes, vol. 24, no. 40), we demonstrated that the order of L2 convergence for the truncated SD method can be very near to 1/2. This work also proves that the truncated SD method maintains the stability properties of the underlying SDE. Inspired by a practical illustration, we introduce a new SD scheme, which we label as the Lamperti semi-discrete (LSD) method, by applying the Lamperti transformation on the initial SDE. Computational experiments corroborate these theoretical results.

John Dalton's initial atomic theory proposed that all elements consist of single atoms, and the atoms in compounds typically exhibit the simplest atomic proportions. An illustration of this idea is Dalton's belief that water's chemical formula was HO, implying an atomic mass for oxygen eight times greater than hydrogen (rather than the current approximation of approximately 16). However, in 1805, Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac and Alexander von Humboldt demonstrated that water comprises two volumes of hydrogen and one volume of oxygen. By 1811, Amedeo Avogadro had accurately interpreted water's structure using what we now know as Avogadro's law and the concept of diatomic molecular entities. [a]

With the rise of cheap small "Cube Satellites," startups are now taking photos and infrared images of factories, retail parking lots, oil tankers, and more and selling these images to customers who want to spy on their competitors, or gain intelligence in other ways. This is not an entirely new phenomenon - the U.S. government has long used satellites to spy on its enemies - but it is becoming increasingly accessible and affordable for private companies and individuals. "It's the democratization of satellite imagery," said Max Chalfin, co-founder and CEO of Terra Bella, a Google subsidiary that sells satellite images to businesses. Terra Bella operates a fleet of seven satellites, each the size of a mini fridge, that circle the Earth every 90 minutes and take high-resolution photos of specific locations that customers request. The company then sells these photos for 1,000 to 5,000 each. Chalfin said the company's customers include oil and gas companies that use the images to track the location of their tankers, retailers that use them to count the number of cars in their competitors' parking lots, and construction companies that use them to track the progress of projects. "People are using this data for all sorts of interesting applications," he said. Another company, Planet Labs, operates a fleet of more than 100 small satellites, called "Doves," that take lower-resolution images of the entire Earth every day. The company sells these images to customers such as farmers, who use them to track the growth of their crops, and mining companies, who use them to track the progress of their operations. "What we're really enabling is a new generation of decision-makers who have access to this data that they never had before," said Will Marshall, co-founder and CEO of Planet Labs. The market for commercial satellite imagery is expected to grow from 2.3 billion in 2015 to 6.7 billion by 2025, according to a report by the research firm MarketsandMarkets. This growth is being driven by the falling cost of launching and operating satellites, as well as the increasing demand for images of Earth from businesses and governments. "It's a very exciting time to be in the satellite industry," said Chalfin.

Young individuals aged 15 to 24 comprise 14% of the populace but contribute approximately 30% to the expenses of motor vehicle mishaps. Since those under 15 cannot legally drive, it is young drivers who are responsible for overdoubling the number of road incidents compared to older generations. Several reasons explain this disproportionate impact: inexperience with alcohol leads to underestimation of consequences, fewer than half (54%) buckle up as per a 2011 survey, teens frequently travel with passengers, and their attention is frequently diverted, increasing the risk of injuries. Considering the safety concerns, I propose delaying the age at which youths are permitted to operate such hazardous machinery until they reach adulthood.

On the other hand, seniors above the age of 75 represent a smaller percentage of the population but account for an alarmingly close rate of traffic collisions and fatalities. Although older drivers exhibit a minimal rate of traffic infringements and the highest seatbelt usage, they face challenges like health issues, diminished motor skills, poor eyesight, and limited neck mobility that hinder their ability to monitor blind spots effectively. By eliminating the two most dangerous demographics of drivers on our roads, we could significantly reduce the overall accident rates.

Interrogations had extended for weeks, growing increasingly arduous in the past fortnight, a series of scars on his back serving as proof. Yet, there he was, confronting the guard who delivered the message, armed with something far more menacing than words. A sudden explosion snapped him out of his musings and spurred him into motion. Seizing a weapon, he barked, "Show the way then." Amidst the chaos of shouts and footsteps from the guards patrolling above, they made their way through the labyrinthine corridors and staircases of the complex. At regular intervals, they paused and waited for their pursuers to pass before continuing their journey towards the main exit. This was a broad corridor leading to a security checkpoint, where two guards stood guard and the door could only be unlocked using a keycard one of them possessed, though Duncan did not know which one. A number of factors are contributing to an oversupply of oil in the global market. The US is ramping up domestic production through methods like hydraulic fracking, aiming to reduce reliance on imports. OPEC, comprised mainly of Middle Eastern oil suppliers, perceives this as a threat and has responded with a price war to maintain market share by flooding the market with oil. Key players in this strategy include Saudi Arabia, whose actions have led to historically low oil prices. Consequently, these low prices have caused significant economic challenges for countries such as Russia, which heavily rely on oil exports for revenue. Additional context: This price war has worsened Russia's economic downturn due to both international sanctions over its actions in Crimea and the decreased revenue from oil sales. Furthermore, seasonal factors, such as reduced demand during winter months and subsidized heating oil, along with unexpectedly high US production levels, have exacerbated the oversupply situation.

The Agency was the subject of [this ethnographic study] (URL0) which details the peculiarities of the IC which impact overall effectiveness. I urge you to read it all, it's really quite fascinating and actually a fairly breezy read. Chief among these peculiarities (not really peculiar as all organizations - government bureaus, large corporations, sports teams, etc, develop their own distinct cultures, mores and languages over time) are: - Extreme insularity. CIA employees set themselves apart from civilian life, see their mission as being of utmost, life-or-death importance (which it is in some cases), and systematically exclude outsiders to the organization. This trickles down to their treatment of new hires, who must "earn" their way up within this rigidly hierarchical and exclusive organization. - An almost hilarious reliance on acronyms and jargon which a) contribute further to the systematic exclusion of outsiders and newbies, b) are employed by veteran personnel to make vague their intentions to others and in doing so further their own personal agendas within the CIA, and c) contributes to the embarrassing overall phenomenon of impenetrable linguistic structures which, when deconstructed, are revealed to be essentially meaningless. For example, the dissertation cites this email subject line: "FYI FOR SA RE: OBE SITREP - NAR AFAIK," which, in IC speak, means "For your information for situational awareness regarding the obsolete situation report - no action required as far as I know." In plain English, this means "nothing happened, no need to do anything." Now, that is pure comedy gold. - Another, related phenomenon is that these linguistic structures bullshit are employed in an atmosphere of extreme interpersonal and professional competitiveness, which leads to what the author depicts as a culture of oneupsmanship. No situation is ever satisfactorily explained as individuals compete with one another to clarify everything said aloud or written until the point where what was originally said is meaningless. Another example, this time of analysts explaining the rules of baseball: "Analyst A: So there are four bases Analyst B: Well, no, it's really three bases plus home plate. Analyst A:.... Okay, three bases plus home plate. The batter hits the ball and advances through the bases one by one - Analyst C: Well, no, it doesn't have to be one base at a time." There's another example in the text of analysts being asked to justify their actions and words endlessly, to the point where "it becomes difficult to say anything definitively without being challenged - often at the expense of the true purpose of the interaction." - One more reason why the IC is dysfunctional is that the job requires effective employees to function as "robots" in order to get through their day. Being repeatedly exposed to violence and carnage and images of violence and carnage, the weight and stakes of the mission and the competitiveness of the organization require analysts to affect an inhuman disposition, which has obvious consequences for people's personal and professional lives. - Information overload, the direct result of so many intelligence pipelines being opened to analysts as a result of post-911 legislation combined with - Stovepiping of intelligence (the separation of information into separate stacks in separate databases) which needlessly complicates the actual acquisition of useful intelligence. In short, the intelligence community suffers from a variety of maladies that hamper its ability to operate effectively, including an exclusive, opaque and purposefully impenetrable professional and social hierarchy, a surfeit of jargon which muddies the waters of personal and professional interaction, a workplace culture where analysts must affect extraordinary stoicness in the face of the absolute worst kinds of violence and stress, and IT practices which are in direct competition with the amount of information they are mandated to sift through. I hope this was helpful and I urge you again to read the paper I cited, because it really is a great peek inside of an organization that very few of us are allowed to be a part of.

In this paper we present a framework for secure identification using deep neural networks, and apply it to the task of template protection for face authentication. We use deep convolutional coding (DSC) as an example to describe the implementation principles of most types of IDF data protection schemes. A target dataset containing faces is also revealed in the randomization process. As shown by an asymmetric algorithm, face recognition may be implemented with multiple architectures and can either expose face information from different types of candidates or provide other forms of identity verification. Targeted masking techniques are used to enhance identity verification and predict which candidate will have the best face. There has been increasing interest in developing high performance modern machine learning algorithms based on error correction technology developed through the intersection between machine learning and security. The general purpose, object classification algorithms (A.P. algorithm) are often used in solving problem learning problems to avoid false positives that could arise due to errors in inference operations. These systems can cause errors concerning the accuracy of matching objects, resulting in incorrect predictions. In contrast to many prior art methods, which rely solely on a pure object classification algorithm, we consider the use of a computational model. To measure convergence, we explore how we implement a single approach by exploring the applicability of a set of large-scale computational models. Using multivariate statistical analysis, we show that a new consensus algorithm, presented with a similarity index of 20, is able to detect the agreement among the A.P. and parallelized concurrency algorithms on average. This results in an additional independent inverse correlation between the two. Our solution provides consistent, low cost efficient optimization solutions suitable for specific applications.

"Ah man, it smells like death in here." That is the phrase that I have lived to regret ever since they fell foolishly from my mouth. I was essentially immortal before that moment in time. I was the best comedian in the world, and apparently better than anyone in the afterlife as well. It was the only reason the Grim Reaper decided not to take me. I could make him laugh, and in his line of work that was a rarity. I don't even remember what it was that I had said when he showed up at my car accident. I can recall him bending down next to my overturned Honda civic and reaching in to pull me out. I made some off the wall comment and he froze, dead in his tracks. It was the weirdest laugh I had ever heard, but one I appreciated more than all of the others combined. He let me live, provided that every year on the anniversary of what should have been my death, I would tell him a joke that would make him cry with laughter. I was his own personal jester, and for that he rewarded me handsomely. And then on that fateful day, 121 years later, I muttered those stupid words that seized our contract and ripped it in two. Who knew Death would be so self conscious about his smell? And to make things worse, that wasn't even the joke that I was going to tell him! The actual joke was a masterpiece, but he wouldn't give me the chance to tell it. I ran out of that room faster than I'd ever run before. And I've been running ever since. I think the reason that he hasn't taken me yet is because of our long history together. That isn't to say that he's forgiven me. He seems to enjoy reminding me that he's near. Everyone I get close to dies without reason. I'll see a dog in the park that I think looks adorable and before I can pet it, it'll fall over dead. Roses crumble before I can enjoy their scent and food rots on my fork before I can bring it to my mouth. He's killing everything around me. I have discovered that Death is a jester of a different sort. I had provided him with a form of humor that he wasn't used to, but he has since grown tired of it, and reverted to his old ways. Now, he once again deals in jokes of cruelty and irony. In a way, I am still fulfilling my part of our old deal. The Reaper still laughs, and he still laughs at me. Only now, the difference is I'm not laughing.

Most common food sources originate from plants that generate food through photosynthesis, or from animals fed by these plants. Photosynthetic organisms, including plants, serve as the foundation of many food webs due to their ability to harness solar energy and soil/atmospheric nutrients, transforming them into consumable forms. This process is recognized as the first trophic level by ecologists. Modern varieties of staple foods, like corn, rice, wheat, legumes, and bananas/plantains, along with fiber crops such as flax and cotton, have evolved from ancient, wild ancestors possessing desirable traits as a result of selective breeding throughout history. Plant scientists focus on understanding plant nutrition and improving crop yields, contributing significantly to humanity's capacity to feed the population and ensure long-term food security. Their research encompasses weed management, as well as plant pathogen biology and control in both agricultural settings and natural ecosystems. Ethnobotany examines the connections between people and plants; when exploring historical plant-human relationships, it is often labeled archaeobotany or palaeoethnobotany.

Think of Iraq and Afghanistan - their crystal ball is often as muddy as yours or mine. While the 2010 Strategic Defence Security Review (SDSR) did identify terrorism and international military crises as high level (tier 1) threats, there was no specific mention of Russia and so-called Islamic State (IS) did not exist in anything like its present form. The 2015 SDSR will identify both IS and Russia as tier 1 threats, but they may not be the same threat five years hence. They say that armies train to fight the last war they fought and military plans don't survive the first contact with the enemy. "In 2010 it was rather assumed the armed forces would get out of Afghanistan and take a bit of a breather," says Michael Clarke, director of the defence think tank Rusi. Instead "the world has shown us the armed forces won't be getting a holiday," he says. First, the government should be commended on its commitment to carry out a defence review every five years. Before, defence reviews were done ad hoc. But ministers will still have to overcome a high degree of scepticism as to whether this latest SDSR is genuinely "strategic" or if it matches Britain's global ambitions with the resources needed. SDSR 2010 may have been strategic in name but it'll be remembered for the savage cuts that followed. It wasn't just the scrapping of iconic names, it left gaping holes in Britain's defences - with no aircraft carriers for the Royal Navy and no maritime patrol aircraft to hunt down Russian submarines. Full document The Royal Navy also lost thousands of personnel and is now having to recruit marine engineers from foreign navies. In order to man its two new aircraft carriers it'll need another 2,000 sailors but they'll have to manage with fewer, which could mean mothballing other warships. The armed forces are still licking the wounds inflicted by the 2010 review. Defence Secretary Michael Fallon admits it involved "painful" decisions. But this week he told me: "We're now able to expand the defence budget again.... to enhance the capabilities of our armed forces to deal with the increased threats we face." Key to this, he says, has been the commitment to meet the Nato target of spending 2 of the nation's wealth (GDP) on defence. It means there'll be a modest increase in the defence budget over the next five years. Mr Clarke says while the armed forces might be in a better place this time round "it'll still find it difficult to meet all the commitments the government wants it to meet." New maritime patrol aircraft will be top of the shopping list. Over the past five years Britain has had to call on the help of the US, Canada and France to hunt for suspected Russian submarines near UK waters. RAF crews have already been training on the US Boeing P8 Poseidon - but it's expensive. Other defence contractors are offering cheaper alternatives. Britain needs new aircraft now, but it has to work out what it can afford. The RAF will also be looking for more frontline fast-jet squadrons. It now has seven squadrons but would like more than a dozen. In the fight against IS it's still having to rely on the ageing Tornado. The life of some of the early Typhoons is likely to be extended to add a few more squadrons, but still probably fewer than the RAF would like. One key decision will be how many of the new F-35s Britain will buy. The aircraft, also known as the Joint Strike Fighter, is already the most expensive defence project ever undertaken by the Pentagon. The UK had originally planned to buy 138, but each jet will cost about PS100m. The decision on F-35s is also important for the Royal Navy and its two new aircraft carriers from which they will fly, as are new anti-submarine frigates needed to protect the carriers. The Navy wants 13 of the new Type 26 frigate. If it has to settle for less that would have a knock-on effect on shipbuilding jobs on the Clyde. The government will also signal its push to renew the fleet of Vanguard submarines which carry the Trident nuclear systems. The cost of building four new submarines will be updated from around PS20bn to more than PS30bn. The Army will be looking at how many new armoured "scout" vehicles they'll be getting and new Apache attack helicopters. Although the Army has become less likely to engage in any large-scale conflict on its own, it still needs a range of capabilities to deploy alongside its key ally - the US. The Army also hopes this SDSR will help change public perceptions - that it's not just there to deploy en masse. The Army now sends small teams to trouble spots all over the world to help train and assist fragile states with conflict prevention. The number of regular troops is shrinking, from 163,000 in 1978 to 102,000 in 2010 and 82,000 in 2020 The government has said it does not want whole regiments to be scrapped; some will be merged, others face "salami slicing." The Army will become more reliant on part-time soldiers; the number of reservists will double from 15,000 to 30,000 by 2020 The government says Britain will have an effective, well-equipped fighting force, integrating regulars and reserves Analysts say the Army will have resources for only one major operation at a time and there will be swingeing cuts to support units such as logistics and engineers More on the Army reorganisation In fact, this SDSR will signal a significant break with the past. Mr Clarke says: "What we are seeing is a shift of resources away from fighting major wars towards using the forces in more intelligence-led, cyber-led, Special Forces-led ways for specific operations." The armed forces still want and need their big ticket items like warplanes and warships, but recent events have underlined the shift. In the wake of the Paris attacks, ministers have said the security services will get another 1,900 personnel while there'll be an extra PS1.9bn for cybersecurity and another PS2bn for Special Forces. The RAF will see the size of its drone fleet double to 20. It's a sign the military will be involved in more intelligence-led counter-terrorism operations and an indication that, post-Iraq and Afghanistan, politicians are increasingly reluctant to put "boots on the ground." After the brutal cuts of the last SDSR, ministers hope this one will be a positive story. While the Ministry of Defence is still having to make efficiency savings, it's not being asked to make cuts right across the board like many other government departments. But more important than how the review is regarded by the public, or the armed forces themselves, is how it's interpreted by Britain's allies and enemies.

Conventional approaches to image de-fencing suffer from non-robust fence detection and are limited to processing images of static scenes. In this position paper, we propose an automatic de-fencing algorithm for images of dynamic scenes. We show that the proposed algorithm is robust to degradations in the visual quality of the captured image and can be extended to remove fences in videos. Furthermore, we propose a crowd-sourcing approach to automatically collecting ground-truth data for training and evaluating the proposed algorithm.

Dynamic textures have emerged as a new field of investigation that extends the concept of computer vision to the study of image textures. The aim is to develop novel techniques for the recognition of dynamic textures in images.
