Occasionally a bisyllabic word is written with two characters that contain the same radical, as in hudie "butterfly," where both characters have the insect radical . A notable example is pipa (a Chinese lute, also a fruit, the loquat, of similar shape) - originally written as with the hand radical, referring to the down and up strokes when playing this instrument, which was then changed to (tree radical), which is still used for the fruit, while the character was changed to when referring to the instrument. In other cases a compound word may coincidentally share a radical without this being meaningful.

Rents in economic terms means a return on some input that exceeds its opportunity cost. The classic example is land in the city vs land far from a city, whatever it costs to build and maintain an apartment building. So what about the benefits of land use? It's less expensive than housing investment, as well as people who live here are more likely to invest in themselves while others don't have access to overpriced apartments or share with their families property values due to the lack of affordable housing options surrounding them (at least those directly affected by the city). Also, real estate can be valuable for personal wealth creation versus property value because that helps create jobs; businesses could also benefit if they're able to provide affordable housing where otherwise private developers might not want to compete against each other again financially because there aren't any vacancies outside of the city limits. That said, real estate isn't necessarily cheap either compared to apartments built near downtown Minneapolis, as neighboring communities such as North Minneapolis would need to pay much higher taxes and fees alone worth hundreds of thousands of dollars per month just to keep up with the competition. The impact this has had upon the economy has been considerable: The city spent 200 million replacing aging streetscape improvements on the east side last year - a project that could easily fund itself through a new tax credit program funded entirely locally controlled by the city. It should come as no surprise that land prices at the center of Minneapolis have fallen dramatically since the city launched the City Council's Land Use Zoning Review Commission two years ago despite the city being one of only five cities nationally without land transactions tax incentives, according to a recent report released Wednesday morning by the real estate experts National Farm Bureau Federation. Land transaction approvals under Minnesota Revised Statutes require bids submitted within 90 days prior to sales price estimation beginning Oct 1st. Land deals deliver payments between 20 and 50, depending on how close to your hometown you reside. A construction contract requires approval from the city council before the company can install structures above 20 feet tall onto the parcel owned by the owner. Land transactions occur when construction contracts expire, causing land owners to relinquish ownership rights later in the process after the purchase agreement expires. But all real estate transfers must pass through a commission established by the commission's members which pays out grants based solely on factors including buyer satisfaction associated with a deal approved and customer satisfaction. Land transactions go beyond that threshold amount into consideration as long as a developer agrees to pay the full compensation cost, including permitting costs and paving costs. These calculations include land acquisition costs like capital improvement projects, purchasing permits required for street repairs executed overseas and relocation expenses incurred during operations inside the city limits. Minnesota's Land Transaction Tax Credit Program annually receives statewide funding totaling 63 billion across the state but it doesn't cover all development purchases, such as roads, sidewalks and parks. Land deals fall outside this definition so reporting requirements vary greatly among municipalities nationwide, especially considering Minnesota does not pay for public transportation services currently. The city still needs federal assistance to finance an influx of new affordable housing units slated to arrive soon via the Minnesota Housing Fund. The city already received 29 million invested back homebuyers last year and has committed additional money toward affordable rentals needed for residents displaced by the COVID-19 pandemic. The city will also receive 22 million to help pay down existing debts stemming from the pandemic recession caused by the pandemic. However, the grants won't translate instantly enough once the apartments open next spring unless representatives from other jurisdictions agree to waive passage fees, which is currently set to expire June 30th 2021. Once those loans start paying off and income begins flowing, Minneapolis can expect to add another 180 rental units along with new homes purchased in the coming months thanks to the city's 5 million Housing Trust Fund.

This paper derives a closed-form method for computing hybrid force-velocity control. The key idea is to maximize the kinematic conditioning of the mechanical system, which includes a robot, free objects, a rigid environment and contact constraints. The method is complete, in that it always produces an optimalnear optimal solution when a solution exists. It is efficient, since it is in closed form, avoiding the iterative search of previous work . We test the method on 78,000 randomly generated test cases. The method outperforms our previous search-based technique by being from 7 to 40 times faster, while consistently producing better solutions in the sense of robustness to kinematic singularity. We also test the method in several representative manipulation experiments.

Tesla was 6 feet 2 inches (1.88 m) tall and weighed 142 pounds (64 kg), with almost no weight variance from 1888 to about 1926.:292 He was an elegant, stylish figure who loved good clothes and enjoyed buying clothes for himself as well as his friends.:262, 264 At the Astor House he was often seen in formal evening wear.:143 At times Tesla was a vegetarian, but at times he was not: he often dined on chicken and other white meats.:294 Tesla walked eight to ten miles each day, and he averaged 175 miles per month.:268 Tesla never smoked tobacco or used alcohol,:281, 282 although he once admitted to experimenting with opium in his youth. Tesla's diary contains an entry which states, "Went to bed with brain ache. Unbounded happiness of the last few days has vanished." Tesla was an occasional visitor to other women's apartments, but these were primarily social calls. Tesla was an ardent fan of swimming, and said he thought he was the first American to swim a mile.:282 Tesla had a lifelong passion for pigeons, which he used in his experiments on mechanical flight and considered an ideal vehicle for carrying messages. Tesla claimed he once took care of a wounded bird that, after he nursed it back to health, followed him around the laboratory for the rest of its life.:282 Tesla was also a fan of pigeon racing, a sport that was at its height in the 1890s. Tesla wrote many articles for magazines and journals. Among his achievements, Tesla discovered the resonant frequency of the Earth and claimed to have developed a means to project electrical power long distance, with little to no loss across the intervening distance. He never put this last claim into practice, however, and eventually abandoned the idea. His patents included the Tesla coil and alternating current motor. He developed the first wireless-controlled robotic boat, and designed the world's first hydroelectric power plant. He also invented fluorescent lights, the bladeless turbine, and the wireless radio. Tesla is honored in the "Inventor's Hall of Fame" and a unit of magnetic induction is named after him.

Presiding officer Tricia Marwick shed tears after veteran Labour MSP Duncan McNeil bid farewell to the parliament. And she was again visibly emotional after Mr Salmond told the chamber: "It's goodbye from me.... for now." Ms Marwick, Mr Salmond and Mr McNeil are among those standing down as MSPs ahead of the election on 5 May. Mr Salmond, who served as first minister between 2007 and 2014, used his valedictory address to repeat a belief he expressed in his very first speech in the parliament that Scotland was "not divided, but diverse." He said both the country and parliament were on a journey, and added: "Yes we are a country of different views, but we are not divided. There is in fact a broad consensus on the need for this parliament to assume greater responsibility for the governance of Scotland. "And we are definitely stronger - so much stronger - as a result of that." He welcomed the transfer of powers to Holyrood under the Scotland Bill, but again insisted the bill did not fulfil the pledges which he said had been made by unionist politicians in the last days of the referendum campaign. There were lighters moments as Mr Salmond, who was speaking before the Chancellor delivered his UK budget, joked that he was aware that he faced competition from a "major attraction down south today." He then added: "However, on balance, I feel that the champion chase at Cheltenham racecourse will not be overshadowed by my remarks." And the former SNP leader joked that he wished everyone standing in the forthcoming election good luck, "albeit with varying degrees of enthusiasm." He concluded his address by saying: "Let me leave you with these final thoughts - there is no greater honour in public life than to be a member of this parliament. "There is no greater task than to mould the public purpose of Scotland. There is no greater cause than to serve the people of this country. "And so with that it is goodbye from me.... for now." Ms Marwick thanked Mr Salmond for his contribution both as an MSP and as first minister, and added that he had "served the parliament and Scotland with distinction." The presiding officer had earlier been moved to tears by a powerful final speech by Scottish Labour backbencher Duncan McNeil, who is stepping down as an MSP after serving in the parliament since it was established in 1999. Mr McNeil used his address to warn that Holyrood had things to learn from Westminster, particularly with regard to the committee system. He said: "It will be this parliament's responsibility to ensure there is accountability, there is scrutiny and even opposition when that is necessary. "We must ensure we are capable of meeting that challenge, or we will face the consequences." He recalled how former Labour MP Robin Cook came to Holyrood to look at the lessons that could be learned when it came to reforming Westminster. But Mr McNeil said: "It saddens me to say we now have to do a bit of learning from them and how they run their business." Former Scottish Conservative MSP Annabel Goldie is also bowing out of Holyrood. In her speech, she joked she would miss her dealings with Finance Secretary John Swinney, especially "his huge outbursts of faux indignation."

The car's blinkers don't have a predetermined "blink rate" set by a computer. Instead, they function based on a thermal switch (URL0). This component gets heated when an electric current passes through it, causing it to deform and disconnect the circuit, thus stopping the turn signals. Once the switch cools down, it reverts to its original shape and completes the circuit, restarting the process. Consequently, the blink rate is contingent upon the thermal switch's physical attributes and the surrounding vehicle environment. As a result, identical switches in various vehicles may exhibit slight discrepancies in their blinking patterns. Historically, simple electrical mechanisms controlled the operation of blinkers, with current triggering a heating element to move, and current ceasing allowing it to cool and move once more. Minute production variations can influence the behavior of seemingly identical blinkers. Manufacturing these components to tighter specifications would increase costs unnecessarily as there is no compelling reason for them to maintain a consistent rate.

A team of engineers in Korea has designed a new Virtual Reality glove that can create the sensation of touch when manipulating digital objects. VR gloves are not new, but they have been limited to creating animated images on screens using haptic feedback rather than the interaction with real objects. The glove could allow for more realistic interactions between digital items and could be used at home or in the workplace. The team's work is described in "Virtual Reality Gloves without Haptic Feedback," an article recently published in IEEE Transactions on Interactive Technology (IT). They use two metal plates and glue them together to form a base for their device which then contains four motors within it. These move the fingers and wrist within the glove so you feel what is happening as you manipulate your object through the touchscreen controls on your computer monitor. The team also found a way around a limitation - if you don't want fingers moving as quickly, you can turn off the motors. This approach allows the glove to maintain its tactile qualities while being able to function like any other virtual reality glove. It should be possible to design future devices based upon this technology and integrate similar functions into existing controllers, making it much easier for users to manipulate physical objects interactively through VR. A potential application would be the development of virtual assistants such as Siri who could appear in user interfaces by allowing us to link up our electronic gadgets via wi-fi.

Programs designed for coding are equivalent to development environments like an IDE. Initially, these programs resemble Notepad but offer features such as syntax highlighting, bracket counting, and a run button to execute your code. The programming language itself necessitates a compiler. This software converts your composed program into machine language. Originally, compilers were penned in machine language. However, contemporary compilers are authored using high-level programming languages. For instance, the Haskell compiler was initially written in C, but as the language evolved, they began composing the Haskell Compiler using Haskell itself.

Distinction among nearby poses and among symmetries of an object is challenging. In this paper, we propose a unified, group-theoretic approach to tackle both. Different from existing works which directly exploit the symmetry structure of individual objects or their properties, our formulation generalizes the concept of similarity between objects while preserving invariant geometric structures and interacting covariantly with the context in which they are embedded. We first define topological average distance as a function that measures how far each point on a manifold remembers its neighbors. Then we establish the notion of spherical regression metric for surfaces endowed with such averages (i.e., all points). Finally, we prove that sphere regression metrics can be naturally approximated by spherical harmonic functions. Remarkably, the convergence rate of these algorithms depends only on parameter values that characterize the object itself and not on those of its environment. To demonstrate their relevance, we give two examples: relocalization problem for two-dimensional graphs and clustering tasks based on boreal feature vectors extracted at various scales.

Mencap president Lord Rix urged the speaker of the House of Lords to push through legislation allowing those in his situation to be assisted to die. He had previously opposed euthanasia, but in a telephone interview with BBC Radio 4's Today programme said his decision was due to a deterioration in his health which he said was preventing him from dying a peaceful death. He said he had been suffering from Alzheimer's for some time and that he would be happy if he had just two years left to live. His comments were part of a wider debate about assisted suicide and euthanasia in the wake of the death of his friend, the 66-year-old former Conservative MP, Brian Sedgemore, in his home in Oxford. Sedgemore, who had had multiple sclerosis since he was in his 20s, was supported by a physician. Lord Rix said he was hopeful that the House of Lords would give quick consideration to legislation passed by the Commons on assisted dying. He urged the government to respect the wishes of Sedgemore, who had said he would have wished to die in the same way. Lord Rix said: "I have no wish to be a martyr. But I would like to get my message out, which is that I can see there is a pressing need for legislation to allow assisted dying, and that I hope it will be implemented as soon as possible. "I would hate for people to think I was in the same category as Brian Sedgemore. I would never have given him an injection myself, but I can see how it might have come about. The idea of a dose of morphine, possibly with a little bit of codeine, to ease the pain is not totally out of this world. The government should not stand in the way." His comments follow those by Sedgemore's partner of 21 years, Jennifer Green, who said she was shocked by the government's suggestion that the MP's death was "premeditated." "It was a horrible thing to say, really. I would have thought the government would have known Brian and would have known his family. I am shocked they could have come out with a statement like that," Green told the Guardian. Sedgemore, a former parliamentary aide, was a member of the hardline leftwing Social Democratic party before joining the Labour party in 1981. He was MP for Hackney North and Stoke Newington from 1987 to 1997, when he lost to the Lib Dem Lynne Featherstone. In the mid-1990s, Sedgemore campaigned for an assisted-dying bill, which was rejected by the House of Lords. He also campaigned against war in Iraq and had been a key ally of Tony Benn. He had a long-running campaign to promote disabled people's rights, including setting up a network of libraries for the blind, and was vice-president of the disability rights organisation UNITE, which he helped to set up in 1997. In 2009, Sedgemore admitted that he had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in the early 1980s and that his condition had worsened in recent years. According to his family, he died on 11 April and they have decided not to seek a postmortem. This article was amended on 17 April 2011. The original said the Hackney North and Stoke Newington constituency had been held by the Conservatives. This has been corrected.

Debate portals and similar web platforms constitute one of the main text sources in computational argumentation research and its applications. While the corpora built upon these sources are rich of argumentatively relevant content and structure, they also include text that is irrelevant, or even detrimental, to their purpose. In this paper, we present a precision-oriented approach to detecting such irrelevant text in a semi-supervised way. Given a few seed examples, the approach automatically learns basic lexical patterns of relevance and irrelevance and then incrementally bootstraps new patterns from sentences matching the patterns. In the existing args.me corpus with 400k argumentative texts, our approach detects almost 87k irrelevant sentences, at a precision of 0.97 according to manual evaluation. With low effort, the approach can be adapted to other web argument corpora, providing a generic way to improve corpus quality.

The excessive volume of data traffic in modern networks places significant financial pressure on the design of backhaul networks. Creating economical backhaul alternatives is an alluring, yet complex, endeavor. Conventional methods for backhaul systems consist of either radio-frequency (RF) transmissions or optical fibers (OF). Although RF represents an affordable option versus OF, it caters to less intensive data rate demands. An intriguing backhaul alternative is free-space optics (FSO), which provides substantial data rates at a comparatively low expense. Nevertheless, FSO is susceptible to environmental factors like rain, fog, and line-of-sight. This study merges the strengths of RF and FSO and introduces a hybrid RF-FSO backhaul solution. It examines the challenge of minimizing backhaul network costs by selecting among OF or hybrid RF-FSO connections between base stations (BS), ensuring compliance with data rate, connectivity, and dependability prerequisites. Under reasonable assumptions regarding the cost of OF and hybrid RF-FSO links, this study demonstrates that the issue is analogous to a maximum weight clique problem, which can be addressed with manageable complexity. Simulation findings reveal that the suggested approach displays near-optimal functionality, particularly for practical pricing levels of hybrid RF-FSO links.

This activity was largely financed through government loans from abroad, mostly from East European countries; interest on these loans became a burden for the national budget. In 1994 the Kenyan Government introduced legislation to regulate the development and operation of hotels; this led directly to a decline in hotel construction that lasted until 1996. Nevertheless, the number of tourists visiting increased steadily over because Kenya's major civil wars prevented international travel. As such troubled times receded, tourism began increasing once more around 1998. Official statistics indicate that between 2000 and 2005, annual visitor numbers averaged 1.5million in 2004 alone. By contrast, total revenue jumped 30 annually to 1.7 billion in 2006 and 3-year rates average 10. Tourism contributed about 15 percent of exports in 2011. Of particular importance are roughly 2.2 million domestic tourists who visit every year, travelling both within the country and internationally.[8] A further 0.959 million Kenyans visited other African nations in 2010,[1011] with trips to South Africa being the top choice among them.[12] National parks and sanctuaries are also popular destinations. Wildlife viewing ranks second only to safaris in attracting visitors to their natural environments. National Parks contribute significantly to employment opportunities and income generation for local communities. Nearly 60 of all jobs in Nairobi come directly or indirectly related to wildlife protection activities. From 2001 to 2009, Tanzania and Zambia were identified by the World Travel Organization as among the world leaders in providing high value-added safari experiences.[13] These two countries have long been known for offering excellent game viewing but have not traditionally played well with western tourists due to political instability and wariness regarding disease transmission. The lion population is estimated to be 700 - 1000 individuals with approximately 100 lions roaming areas outside national park boundaries. With the establishment of coalition rangers including private volunteers, poaching levels decreased.[15] Despite these efforts, some experts argue that illegal ivory trade continues,[16] particularly between Somalia[17] and neighbouring states. In this study, we introduced T-Net, featuring an embedded encoder-decoder within an encoder-decoder architecture (EDiED). T-Net addresses the constraint that U-Net has just one conjunction layer between the encoder and decoder module. Specifically, U-Net uniformly places the fusion layers, resulting in the encoder's lower-level characteristic merging with the decoder's later stages, and the higher-level trait connecting to its initial stages. T-Net designs the pooling and deconvolution operations suitably throughout the encoding and decoding processes, generating feature maps of assorted sizes within a solitary block. This arrangement ensures that all encoder features, ranging from low-level to high-level, are transferred from the decoder's onset to generate a more precise mask. For evaluating T-Net, we addressed the task of segmenting the three major vessels in coronary angiography images. The assessment included comparing U-Net and T-Nets under identical circumstances and optimizing T-Net for main vessel segmentation. Ultimately, T-Net achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) score of 0.815, a 0.095 improvement compared to U-Net, while the optimized T-Net secured a DSC of 0.890, representing a 0.170 enhancement over U-Net. Furthermore, we exhibited the convolutional layer's weight activation for T-Net and U-Net to validate that T-Net anticipates the mask from earlier decoders. Based on these findings, we anticipate that T-Net will prove beneficial for tackling comparable medical image segmentation challenges.

Charon gently paddled the long oar across the dark waters, silence his only companion in the foggy waters of Styx. He craned his bony neck as he stared off into the mist and rain, listening for any sound that would indicate the presence of a soul. He knew it would not be easy. The grief-stricken, the weeping, the tortured, the angry and confused all came to the river, but none were always ready to step off the bank into the boat and on to the next life. No one knew this better than Charon, who had been ferrying the dead to the underworld for countless centuries. Some souls were stubborn, preferring to cling to the belief that there was something else waiting for them when they reached the end of the journey. There was no explanation for their disbelief, no reason for their fear. Charon did not judge them, simply did his duty, waiting patiently, determined to carry out the task until the last breath had been exhaled. For a thousand years, he had been waiting. He had ferried souls from every corner of the Earth, from the great cities of Rome and Paris, from the vast expanses of the plains of Russia and the steaming jungles of the Far East, from the icy tundras of the Arctic to the steamy jungles of the Amazon. He had ferried souls from the battlefields of the American Civil War and the trenches of World War I. From the beaches of Normandy, the shores of Guadalcanal, the fields of Vietnam and the deserts of the Gulf War. He had ferried souls from the World Trade Center on 911. He had seen many wars, many natural disasters, and the death of millions of souls. It was hard for him to believe he was still waiting. The long oar dipped into the water with a barely perceptible splash. Charon's ears twitched, and he stared through the misty fog. He heard it again, a little louder this time. There was nothing he could do but wait. He had a boat full of souls, and while he would not force them to leave the comfort of the world they knew, he would have to wait for the boat to empty before he could go in search of the one who called to him. He waited, listening to the gentle lapping of the waters against the sides of the boat. He had been waiting for more than a thousand years. He waited for what seemed like an eternity. He looked up at the dark clouds hanging low over the waters. Rain began to fall, and Charon cowered slightly in the bottom of the boat, letting the water run down his face and neck. He closed his eyes, and felt the dampness seeping into his bones. When he opened them again, the darkness was gone. The clouds had cleared and the fog had lifted, and the waters of Styx were clear and bright in the morning sun. Charon looked down into the bottom of the boat. They were all gone. He looked over at the bank, and saw a lone figure standing there. He could barely make him out, but he recognized him. He had waited so long for this moment. Charon stood up and began to walk toward the bank. He reached the edge of the boat and extended a bony hand to help the soul step out of the boat. It had been such a long time since he had carried a soul. He would not make that mistake again. The man looked back at Charon and gave him a small smile, then began to walk up the bank. Charon nodded and smiled. He had waited so long. He had finally ferried a soul. A recent study by the National Institute of Dairy and Frozen Treats (NIDFT) has uncovered the key to keeping ice cream creamy, not crunchy. The scientists at NIDFT conducted a series of tests to determine what factors contributed to ice cream becoming crunchy. After months of experimentation and analysis, they concluded that it was the presence of air bubbles in the mixture that caused the ice cream to lose its creaminess. The team discovered that the best way to prevent ice cream from becoming crunchy was to reduce the amount of air bubbles in the mixture. This could be done by stirring the ice cream slowly while it is being churned. The slower the stirring, the less air bubbles would be incorporated into the mixture and the creamier the end result. The researchers also determined that the temperature at which the ice cream was stored also had an effect on its texture. Ice cream should be stored at -17C in order to keep it creamy for longer. The findings from this study will help people everywhere enjoy their favorite frozen treats for longer. With the right techniques and storage conditions, you can enjoy scoop after scoop of creamy, delicious ice cream without having to worry about it going stale or turning crunchy.

Environmental determinism provided a ethical rationale for the subjugation of specific lands and populations. To depart from Earth, it is essential to attain escape velocity, which decreases as you ascend (in contrast, for entering orbit, you must remain below it). This is because a slower rocket can eventually surpass escape velocity by descending far enough to drop beneath its speed, failing to do so would result in its return or orbital capture. However, practical considerations often dissuade us from this approach. Among these reasons is the additional fuel required to elevate each unit of fuel, necessitating an early expenditure of fuel to decrease the overall mass that needs to be raised. Although many rockets initially accelerate gradually to minimize drag, their initial acceleration is significantly faster than any perceived motion in everyday life. From a physical perspective, there is no impediment to escaping Earth gradually due to escape velocity's dependence on altitude. By climbing higher, you can achieve escape velocity with a lower speed. Essentially, a ball thrown vertically upward from a greater height requires less initial velocity to escape Earth's gravity. However, this discussion pertains specifically to escape velocity, while reaching the edge of space, typically considered around 62 miles or 100 kilometers, involves distinct considerations.

It was a necessary chore, attending these sessions. Without a minimal functional certification of mental health, he would lose access to the colony's automated systems, the only thing now keeping him alive. It was just one of the hoops he had to jump through, and by far his least favourite. "Hello again..... Technician Chang." The waxy mannequin face of the therapeutic droid jerked creepily into life as its tinny voice ran through the same pre-recorded lines. "How are you feeling today?" "Just fine, doc." His reply came through a strained smile, carefully ticking all the boxes in the droid's mental health and wellbeing checklist. "A little lonely, but I keep active." "Why do you think you are..... lonely?" "Oh I don't know, doc. I think it's something to do with that meteor shower killing everyone else in the colony, you remember?" The droid's head tilted slightly in a mimicry of thoughtfulness. "You have spoken of this before..... The system shows no record of such an event." "Well no, not after the mainframe was smashed to pieces by all that space rock. It's a miracle anything survived." "Do you consider yourself..... divine..... Technician Chang?" "No," he sighed. "Just unlucky. It's not that kind of miracle." He rubbed his face, already fatigued by the talk. "Can we just skip to the part where you diagnose me with colonist isolational delusional disorder and give me my partial systems access for the month?" The droid's head tilted to the side again erratically. "There is no need for hostility..... Technician Chang." He threw up his hands, suddenly afraid. "No hostility, doc, no hostility." He beamed, manically, in an attempt at friendliness. "Everybody's calm here. Please continue. I'm cooperating." The remainder of the session continued as normal, he answered the droid's questions about his habits succinctly, his voice draining of life with every question. When it was done, he snapped up his systems access and quick marched out of the wellness assessment room toward the mess and his monthly ration of alcohol, fuming and miserable, as he always did. The droid waited a moment, until a section of wall behind it slid to one side and turned to greet the men in white coats much more smoothly than it had moved before Chang. Its voice was more sophisticated and less mechanical now, very nearly human, with that undertone of silicon that was mandated for almost all humanoid constructs. "The subject is showing more strain with every session, doctors, as I'm sure you've seen." "Yes," said the foremost of the scientists as he distractedly scribbled on a notepad. "Yes, it is fascinating. The machine is utterly convinced that it's human, with all the human frailties." He turned to his colleagues. "Soon we'll see if an AI can go insane."

I love her like she's my daughter and it's been so good to watch her grow up, but sometimes I feel like I have two children and I feel like one of them is missing," she said. The story of how the syndrome came to light has become something of a myth. One story is that the eye was discovered when the owner of a boat was floating in the water and the eye came into view. "I'm not sure how that story got started," said Dr. Joan Werth, an ophthalmologist at the University of Minnesota Medical Center who is also the PIO. "I do know that I remember having a patient with this, and I think it's very rare," she said. According to Dr. Werth, about 10 to 20 cases of sclerocornea have been documented in the medical literature. It is estimated that about 1 in 10,000 people have it. "The number of people who are affected by this is really very small," she said. The most common symptoms are distorted vision, double vision and decreased vision. If the disease progresses, there may be pain and problems with seeing near objects. Dr. Werth says that because of the condition, the person who has sclerocornea will have trouble seeing well in bright light and poor contrast vision. It is not a disease that affects the entire eye. "It affects one eye and the person has a slightly different appearance. They have a cataract in the other eye," she said. "There's no one way to describe it. It's hard to see if it's really one eye or two eyes. It's not the same person." In her case, she was first diagnosed with sclerocornea in 1976. Her ophthalmologist found that the eye was attached to the cornea but that the iris was missing. She had been living with the eye for 10 years before it was found. Dr. Werth said that it was the right thing to do to remove the eye. "I was concerned that if I didn't remove it that she would continue to have pain and problems and not be able to see. I did not want to keep her eye in. I thought it was a good decision," she said. The condition was discovered when she was 10 years old. She went to the University of Minnesota Medical Center because she had been experiencing blurred vision and was concerned about her vision. "The reason that I went to the University of Minnesota was because my ophthalmologist was from there. He had worked with them before. He recommended that I go to the University of Minnesota," she said. The eye was removed at the University of Minnesota Medical Center and the sclerocornea was repaired. "I was the first case in the world that was removed and repaired," she said. She was in her early 20s when she had the surgery. The eye is in her head and will never be replaced. "It's kind of a quirk in my life," she said. "I can't see very well and I have to wear glasses. I'm not happy about that, but I can see. I don't know what I'd do without my glasses." Now, the eye is part of her history. "I have it on my shelf. I look at it every day," she said.

Modern web tech developments facilitate personalized proxies, enabling users to fulfill intricate info monitoring and amalgamation requirements via continuous queries of assorted fluctuating data sources. These proxies encounter a scalability hurdle when aiming to accommodate a high client load without compromising on catering to their intricate user specifications. This research applies a Complex Execution Interval (CEI) abstraction derived from Simple Execution Intervals (EIs) as a representation of user profiles, utilizing existing offline approximation as a reference for optimally capturing CEIs. Three heuristic methods for online query scheduling to fulfill intricate user profiles are proposed. The initial method solely takes into account characteristics of single EIs; the subsequent two approaches leverage traits of all EIs within a CEI. Experimental analysis using authentic data sets and artificial data demonstrates that heuristics capitalizing on CEI insights prevail under diverse parameter configurations.

Fast Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is highly in demand for many clinical applications in order to reduce the scanning cost and improve the patient experience. This can also potentially increase patient throughput and reduce the need for repeat scans. In the context of this project, the problem of accelerating MRI is treated as an image reconstruction problem, i.e., the main goal is to reconstruct a high-quality image from under-sampled k-space data. This project is a joint collaboration between Dr. Hanjoong Jo and Dr. Haris Vikalo. Dr. Hanjoong Jo is a professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC), and the leader of the Medical Imaging Research Laboratory (MIR Lab). Dr. Haris Vikalo is an assistant professor at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at the University of Iowa (UI). This collaboration brings together the complementary expertise of the two groups in order to address the problem of accelerating MRI. In this project, we propose a novel image reconstruction algorithm for MRI based on the following premise: in order to accelerate MRI, we should capture the sparsity of the image in the spatial domain, and the sparsity of the image in the Fourier domain. Our algorithm is a regularized image reconstruction algorithm. We use the 1-norm of the image to capture the spatial sparsity, and the 1-norm of the Fourier transform of the image to capture the Fourier sparsity. This idea of enforcing sparsity of the Fourier transform of an image is novel. To the best of our knowledge, it has never been employed for the purpose of accelerating MRI. The algorithm is computationally efficient, because it does not require the computation of the Fourier transform of the image. This project is currently funded by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) through the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (NIBIB).

My voice trails off and I don't move, betraying my pleas to go. "Stay," it says, calmer. "It's in your pocket." I look down, my eyes filled with tears. I remove the small bag from my pocket and unzip it. I take out my gear, and place it in my lap. I pull a lighter from my pocket, load up, and begin to cook. I watch the bubbles appear. I hate this. I hate this. I set the spoon down and put a cotton swab in it. Stabbing the needle through, I pull back the plunger, watching the dirty liquid fill the syringe. I tie off my arm, and look for a vein. Kate had always been known for her tough exterior. She was the go-to girl for anyone who needed help, advice, or just a good shoulder to cry on. But deep down, Kate was struggling. One day, Kate's boss piled on one too many responsibilities onto her plate. She didn't want to disappoint anyone, so she took on everything that was asked of her without saying a word. The stress of it all started to pile up, and Kate felt like she was suffocating. On her way home from work, Kate's car broke down on the side of the road. She tried her best to fix it, but it was no use. That was the moment when everything came crashing down. Kate broke down and cried on the side of the road. All of the emotions that she had been bottling up for so long finally came pouring out. She felt helpless, alone, and like she was drowning in her own struggles. It was a wake-up call for Kate. She realized that she needed to start taking care of herself instead of just taking on everyone else's problems. She went to therapy, started practicing self-care, and learned how to say "no" when things became too much to handle. It wasn't an easy journey, but Kate made it through. She learned that it's okay to be vulnerable and to not have everything together all the time. Now, Kate is happier and healthier than ever before, thanks to the breakdown that helped her realize what was truly important in life.

The Philadelphia dialect, which is spread throughout the Delaware Valley and South Jersey, is part of Mid-Atlantic American English, and as such it is identical in many ways to the Baltimore dialect. Unlike the Baltimore dialect, however, the Philadelphia accent also shares many similarities with the New York accent. Thanks to over a century of linguistics data collected by researchers at the University of Pennsylvania, the Philadelphia dialect under sociolinguist William Labov has been one of the best-studied forms of American English.[f]

Although face-to-face interaction enhances productive teamwork, the evolving characteristics and organization of team communication remain largely unexplored. In our research, we integrate sociometric analysis from Rhythm Badge sensors with two visualization methods (Dynamic Complexity Heat Maps and Network Representations) to improve the comprehension of team interaction dynamics. We substantiate the worth of our methodology through a case study analyzing the communication of a single team during a Lost at Sea simulation. Our findings indicate that we successfully recapture shifts in tasks and team interaction. Furthermore, we expose alterations in the energy and involvement of team members and represent them graphically within networks. Collectively, this investigation signifies a significant initial phase in pinpointing pivotal transition moments in team communication and interpersonal trends, laying the groundwork for potential future studies aimed at improving team productivity and welfare.

After learning about electricity from Edison's patents in 1882, he decided to pursue his own invention based upon them instead. Tesla focused mainly on electric current measurements using electromagnets and inductive coils; these were used as an alternative means of measuring alternating currents without sampling the signal. During this period, Tesla first coined the term "electronic phase" or "phase shift" to refer to a measure of voltage, rather than frequency due to a capacitance effect. The use of such terms allowed him to continue building his knowledge of electrical theory by looking up various papers written over time using the proper terminology. In 1890, Tesla published a paper describing what is now known as the modern phase shift method for measuring AC power flows through transformers. While Tesla may not have been particularly innovative with his early experiments (he could still be credited with the technical basis for AC induction), his pioneering use of the then-new technology that went into the development of DC motors made him the patriarch of the field of permanent magnet synchronous motors, which dominated motoring drive train technologies until the introduction of direct-current machines around 1980. The issue of individuals occupying abandoned homes, often referred to as "squatters," initially piqued my interest through this reddit post [linked here]. I was shocked to learn that such individuals could trespass into empty dwellings and establish claims, shielded by the law. Upon further investigation, however, I discovered that the problem wasn't about squatters' rights (though it exists under the term "adverse possession," which I still find objectionable). Instead, the intruder had alleged a verbal agreement. Despite both parties denying such an arrangement, this classification makes it a civil dispute, leaving the police powerless to act. I advocate for a legal revision that favors the homeowner to protect property and prevent vandalism and theft, damages the homeowner may never recoup. While the squatters were eventually evicted, they left behind a devastated dwelling. If the homeowner pursued a lawsuit for property damage, they were unlikely to receive compensation. Similar accounts have emerged in comment threads on various articles. In one instance, a law enforcement officer shared a tale of responding to a burglary report. The family, away on vacation for merely three weeks, returned to find squatters residing in their house. When they contacted the authorities, the squatters were initially expelled; however, the District Attorney intervened, allowing them to remain and advising the family that it was a civil matter. By the time a court order was granted for their removal, their possessions were pilfered, and the house's plumbing was wrecked to salvage the copper. In my view, if clear ownership of the residence can be established, the squatters should bear the responsibility of providing proof of a written contract, duly authorized by the property owner or appointed representative. The precise and equitable appraisal of scientific productivity and influence remains a persisting challenge, in spite of extensive research endeavors. Multiple approaches exist to gauge the merit and accomplishment of individual researchers and research institutions. The heterogeneous conduct of scientists worldwide complicates the comprehensive analysis of scholarly outputs. Among various bibliometric indicators, the widely-adopted H-index holds significant appeal due to its simplicity and clear meaning. This study employs the underlying concepts of the H-index to examine networks of scientists referenced by publishing authors. An innovative author evaluation metric termed aH-index is suggested, along with its understandable attributes and connotations. Initial investigations into the performance of computer science researchers with high H-indices are provided to showcase the features of the proposed measure.

This article tells the story of how a user ended up losing his important data due to a ransomware attack and what he did to prevent the same from happening again. Before I tell you the story of what happened to me, I would like to tell you about ransomware and what it does. Ransomware is a type of malware that locks a user's files. The files are locked in such a way that they become inaccessible. The malware then presents a screen that asks the user to pay a ransom in order to get back their files. It is usually a crypto currency like Bitcoin. The ransomware then gives a link that can be used to make the payment. After a payment is made, the hacker will release a decryption key that will enable the user to decrypt their files. This malware can be downloaded as an email attachment or by clicking on a link. This story happened about two years ago. I was a second year student at the time. I was a victim of ransomware, and I lost my important files. The malware locked my files, and I had no way of accessing them. When the malware appeared, it demanded that I pay some money to be able to decrypt my files. I had no money at the time and decided to look for another way to decrypt my files. I tried looking for some online tools, but I had no luck. I had to wait for a few days until I came across a site that had a list of ransomware decryption tools. I downloaded a few of them, and they were not able to decrypt my files. I then realized that I had no choice but to pay the ransom. I had no money at the time, but I knew of a friend who could help me out. I asked her for the money, and she helped me out. I paid the hacker, and he sent me a decryption key. This enabled me to decrypt my files. I was very happy that I had gotten back my files. I had no other choice but to pay the ransom. I learned from this experience, and I decided to find a better way to protect my files. I searched online for some software that could help me to recover my files in case the same thing happened. I came across a data recovery software. This software was able to recover my files in the case of a ransomware attack or any other type of data loss. I have been using this software for about two years now, and I can say that I am happy with it. This software is called Disk Drill. It is available for Mac OS X and Windows. There are three versions of this software, and they are: Free, Basic and PRO. Disk Drill is capable of recovering over 200 file formats. This software can recover files from hard drives, USB drives, memory cards, iPods and other devices. This software has a simple user interface and is easy to use. It is also capable of creating an image of a drive or a partition. This software can be used to recover files that have been lost due to ransomware, accidental deletion, OS crash, partition deletion and other data loss scenarios. The free version of Disk Drill is capable of recovering up to 500MB worth of data. The Basic and PRO versions are able to recover unlimited data. I would recommend that you give this software a try. The finding was one of the takeaways from a US central bank survey of more than 6,640 adults published on Friday. In total, the number of respondents with no more than a high-school diploma who said they were "living comfortably" or "doing okay" fell to 60 from 61. Overall, the annual survey showed US economic health improving. Some 70 of respondents said they were either "living comfortably" or "doing okay," up from 69 the year before, and 62 in 2013 when the Federal Reserve started the survey. But there were continuing signs of instability, with over a third of US households (35) saying they could not cover their monthly bills or an unexpected 400 (PS307) expense, according to the survey. The survey also suggested that disparities between households with different education levels was growing. Gap between rich and poor'keeps growing' Enriching the rich in the US - but what about the rest? "A clear pattern over the past two years across these measures is that the improvements have been most pronounced among those with greater levels of education," researchers wrote in the report. Nearly 100 million Americans have no education beyond high school, according to US government estimates. (The estimate excludes members of the military and people in institutional facilities such as prison.) That fact is tied to wide differences, the survey found. About 46 of adults with at least a college degree reported family incomes of 100,000 or more, compared to just 9 of respondents with a high school degree or less. Adults with at least a college degree were more likely to report earning money from online activities - such as renting out properties using a website - and more likely to have a steady stream of income from month-to-month. They were also more likely to say they received a raise in the last year, and more likely to say it exceeded the growth in their expenses. "The thing is that earnings are so highly correlated with education and employment," said Sandy Baum, a senior fellow at the Urban Institute, a Washington think tank. "It's hard to imagine how a sense of financial wellbeing would not be correlated with education." Jobs in sectors that once supplied well-paid work for school leavers, such as manufacturing, have fallen. At the same time, the overall labour market has become more unstable as employers cut back on benefits and pay rises. The share of Americans in the workforce is also shrinking - particularly among those with lower levels of education, said Valerie Wilson, an economist at the Economic Policy Institute. "The workers we would expect to have the strongest labour attachments have actually been becoming less attached," she said. Among survey respondents who did not attend college, nearly 40 said it was too expensive or that they needed to earn money. Their status was also closely tied to whether their parents had attended college. But Ms Baum said simply getting everyone to go to college is not the solution. "There could be more work done to equalise things at the level of higher education but the problem is never going to be solved just at the college level," she said.

Answering these questions requires both data science expertise and strong collaborative relationships across our health system, including national bodies like Health Canada and provincial ministries of health. They must have the ability to collaborate freely with each other while keeping their respective roles separate so as to avoid regulatory challenges. This creates an opportunity for governments to work collaboratively with industry in order to share information quickly without having to resort to ad hoc arrangements or even legislation. However, this type of collaboration needs to continue long after the pandemic crisis ends. Finally, it becomes increasingly clear how important telemedicine has become during the COVID-19 pandemic. The ultimate goal should be to ensure no family ever experiences another lockdown, ensuring all Canadians have access to primary care delivered remotely via video conferencing tools. Telehealth services may increase efficiency but may also improve access to care because of their capacity for geographic reach. Quebec, for example, recently announced plans to expand its telecheck program beyond cancer screening to more complex chronic conditions like diabetes, heart disease and hypertension. Some Canadian jurisdictions have already developed policies to fund telemedical consultations through the public insurance programs. A universal approach would also allow us to better address common barriers to accessing virtual care. Many households lack reliable internet service or high-speed access; others simply cannot afford the devices required for remote medical appointments. Here too, technology offers solutions: phones and tablets can easily connect patients to clinicians who live outside their home community. Similarly, telemedicine platforms can enable physicians to provide care wherever they happen to be located. Technologies like these will require investment, particularly given the scale involved. But even before the pandemic struck, many experts were calling for increased investments to support innovation in digital health technologies. Taken together, there's no question that COVID-19 is accelerating technological change in the Canadian healthcare sector. Now it is up to policy makers to seize the opportunity created by the crisis and act decisively to ensure everyone gets the best possible health-care experience.

I am firmly in the realm of working poor. I believe that the most effective way to improve the economy in the short term would be to subsidize a few specific business types because they are a locus of good effects. Specifically, I support the subsidy of: Drop-off laundry services, house cleaning, dry-cleaning, landscaping, dog-walking, personal shopping, babysitting, house-painting, and there are probably some other jobs that would meet the requirements of the good effects. These seem like strange jobs to subsidize, but the effect I seek is to lower the cost of services that increase leisure time for the working poor, while also being jobs that require low-skill labor. Creating jobs and freeing up people with jobs to have more free time, which can be used to either engage in leisure spending or do more work. I work 60 hours a week plus travel, and that means that I will sometimes have to take a half day off at one of my jobs to do laundry at the laundromat, which is only open during business hours. If I could do a drop- laundry for a much lower price, I would have more time to do more work. I would suggest something like a substantial tax exemption per employee in the business, andor zero-interest business loans.

We propose LETO, a new hybrid Lagrangian-Eulerian method for topology optimization. At the heart of LETO lies in a hybrid particle-grid Material Point Method (MPM) to solve for elastic force equilibrium. LETO transfers density information from freely movable Lagrangian carrier particles to a fixed set of Eulerian quadrature points. The quadrature points act as MPM particles embedded in a lower-resolution grid and enable sub-cell resolution of intricate structures with a reduced computational cost. By treating both densities and positions of the carrier particles as optimization variables, LETO reparameterizes the Eulerian solution space of topology optimization in a Lagrangian view. LETO also unifies the treatment for both linear and non-linear elastic materials. In the non-linear deformation regime, the resulting scheme naturally permits large deformation and buckling behaviors. Additionally, LETO explores contact-awareness during optimization by incorporating a fictitious domain-based contact model into the static equilibrium solver, resulting in the discovery of novel structures. We conduct an extensive set of experiments. By comparing against a representative Eulerian scheme, LETO's objective achieves an average quantitative improvement of 20 (up to 40) in 3D and 2 in 2D (up to 12). Qualitatively, LETO also discovers novel non-linear functional structures and conducts self-contact-aware structural explorations.

I am not a counselor, I'm not a teacher, and I'm not your mom. I am an advice columnist, which means that people write to me with their problems and I give them my opinion. That's it. I'm not a professional, I'm not qualified, and I'm not getting paid for this. I'm just some girl who likes to give advice. So please, don't write to me expecting me to fix your life. I can't. Urine is made up of water and waste products that the body wants to get rid of. Seawater also contains water and waste products, but it also contains salt. [header] How to deal with difficult in-laws [title] Respect your in-law's attachment to your spouse [step] Your spouse is their little boy or girl, and always will be, no matter how grown up. Especially if you have your own young children, think about how difficult it will be to "let them go" as adults someday. This attachment can often lead to difficult behaviors from your in-laws. Therefore, try to be understanding of their perspective and show empathy towards them. Reinforce your in-laws' connection to your spouse by encouraging them to spend time together, even if it doesn't include you. [step] Establish clear boundaries with your in-laws. If certain behaviors or topics of discussion make you uncomfortable, politely let them know. Remember to use "I" statements and avoid placing blame on your in-laws. Respect their boundaries as well, and try to find common ground on what is acceptable for both parties. [step] Keep communication open with your spouse about any issues that arise with their parents. It is important to work together as a team to find solutions and maintain a healthy relationship with your in-laws. Remember, you both have a shared interest in maintaining a positive relationship with them. [step] Lastly, don't be afraid to seek outside help if needed. This can include couples therapy or family counseling. A neutral party can help to provide strategies for managing difficult behaviors and conflicts within the family dynamic.

I remain undecided on the issue of vaccinations. While I don't hold the belief that vaccines cause autism, I acknowledge the validity of certain criticisms. One criticism is that vaccine compositions are proprietary information, leaving consumers unaware of potential immune system altering substances. Another criticism is that the pharmaceutical industry financially benefits from maintaining an ill population. These perspectives, though often deemed conspiratorial, can be compared to the oil industry where monetary gains are tied to non-renewable resources and potential health risks. It is important to note that these views do not align with my own stance. Instead, I find myself uncertain and indecisive regarding vaccinations.
